nehemiah-7:12:1.summary: Lists men “from the sons of Elam” in the mixed-marriage list, the same clan.
nehemiah-7:12:1.why: Same clan in a later list.

nehemiah-7:24:0.summary: Ezra's parallel list gives “the sons of Iora: one hundred and twelve,” the same entry under another name.
nehemiah-7:24:0.why: Parallel entry with the same count.

nehemiah-7:27:1.summary: Jeremiah lived in Anathoth, the town listed here.

nehemiah-7:27:2.summary: Anathoth is named among towns in Isaiah's oracle.

nehemiah-7:27:3.summary: Names “the men of Anathoth,” the same town.

nehemiah-7:29:0.summary: Lists Beeroth among Benjamin's cities, the same town.

nehemiah-7:29:3.summary: Kiriath-jearim, the town Kariathiarim listed here.

nehemiah-7:30:0.summary: Lists Gaba and Ramah among Benjamin's cities, matching Arama and Gabaa.

nehemiah-7:31:0.summary: Machmas appears in Isaiah's oracle, the same town.

nehemiah-7:31:1.summary: Michmash, the same town as Machemas, in Saul's war.

nehemiah-7:31:2.summary: The foreigners camp at Michmash, the same town.

nehemiah-7:32:1.summary: Ai in Joshua's conquest, the town Aia listed here.

nehemiah-7:32:2.summary: Joshua's ambush lies “between Bethel and Ai,” the same pair of towns.

nehemiah-7:34:0.summary: The same figure, “one thousand two hundred fifty-four,” is given for Ailam in the same list.
nehemiah-7:34:0.why: Notes a repeated entry and count.

nehemiah-7:35:0.summary: Lists men “from the sons of Eram,” the same clan.
nehemiah-7:35:0.why: Same clan in a later list.

nehemiah-7:37:0.summary: Shemed “built Ono and Lod,” the same towns.

nehemiah-7:37:2.summary: The enemies propose meeting “in the plain of Ono,” the same place.

nehemiah-7:39:1.summary: The priestly courses include “the ninth for Jesus,” the house named here (truncated).

nehemiah-7:40:0.summary: “The sixteenth for Emmer” is the same priestly family.

nehemiah-7:41:0.summary: Adaia's ancestry includes Paschor, the priestly family Phassour.

nehemiah-7:41:3.summary: Lists men “from the sons of Phasour,” the same priestly family.

nehemiah-7:42:0.summary: “The third for Charem” is the priestly course of Harim, spelled Eram here.

nehemiah-7:42:2.summary: Names “the sons of Eram,” but this list is of laymen, not the priestly family here.

nehemiah-7:43:1.summary: Raphaia, a district ruler, has no link to these Levites.

nehemiah-7:44:1.summary: Names “Asaph's sons,” the same family of singers.

nehemiah-7:45:1.summary: Lists the divisions of temple gatekeepers, background for the gatekeeper families here (truncated).

nehemiah-7:46:0.summary: Lists “the given ones” with priests and Levites, the same class as the Nathinim.

nehemiah-7:46:1.summary: The Gibeonites are made temple woodcutters and water-carriers, often taken as an origin of temple servants (truncated).

nehemiah-7:46:2.summary: Vow valuations have no link to the Nathinim list.

nehemiah-7:57:1.summary: Names “the sons of Salomon's slaves,” the same group.
nehemiah-7:57:1.why: Same group in a later list.

nehemiah-7:63:0.summary: “The sons of Barzillai the Gileadite,” the same family name taken by this priest.

nehemiah-7:63:1.summary: Barzillai the Gileadite, the ancestor whose name this priestly family took.

nehemiah-7:63:3.summary: Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim, the ancestor named here.

nehemiah-7:64:0.summary: All Israel “recorded by enrollment,” a general parallel to genealogical records.

nehemiah-7:64:2.summary: Nehemiah prays about “disqualification by descent from the priesthood,” the same issue.

nehemiah-7:64:3.summary: A guest excluded for lacking the proper garment loosely parallels exclusion for lacking proof.

nehemiah-7:64:4.summary: The Lord saying “I do not know you” loosely parallels exclusion of the unrecorded.

nehemiah-7:64:5.summary: The high priest's sin offering has no link to exclusion by descent.

nehemiah-7:65:3.summary: The shown text names Neemias but not the title Athersatha.

nehemiah-7:65:4.summary: Levi receives “manifestations” and truth, loosely related to the awaited priestly oracle.

nehemiah-7:65:5.summary: The priest asks “the judgment of the manifestations,” loosely related to awaiting a priest for decision.

nehemiah-7:65:6.summary: Priestly offerings are “most holy,” the same holy things these men may not eat.

nehemiah-7:65:10.summary: What remains of the sacrifice is Aaron's sons' and “most holy,” the food withheld here.

nehemiah-7:67:1.summary: God's call of Cyrus has no link to the count of slaves and singers.

nehemiah-7:70:2.summary: Temple vessels made for Solomon broadly parallel gifts of bowls for the work.

nehemiah-7:70:3.summary: Israel's rulers present gifts for the Tent's work, as family heads give for the work here (truncated).

nehemiah-8:1:1.summary: A book of law is found and handed to a scribe, broadly parallel to bringing the law to a scribe.

nehemiah-8:3:7.summary: Eager reception of the word is a general parallel.

nehemiah-8:3:8.summary: Moses being read regularly is a general parallel to public reading of the law.

nehemiah-8:3:9.summary: Prophets read every Sabbath is a general parallel.

nehemiah-8:3:10.summary: Lydia attending to Paul's words is a general parallel to attentive hearing.

nehemiah-8:3:11.summary: Crowds astonished at Jesus' authority has no specific link to this reading.

nehemiah-8:3:12.summary: “The reading of the law” in the synagogue is a general parallel.

nehemiah-8:3:13.summary: Paul expounds “the law of Moses” from morning until evening, a parallel long session on the law.

nehemiah-8:3:14.summary: A crowd listening gladly is a general parallel.

nehemiah-8:3:15.summary: Paul talking long into the night loosely parallels a long reading session.

nehemiah-8:3:16.summary: Paul prolonging his message until midnight loosely parallels a long reading.

nehemiah-8:4:2.summary: A Mesoulam among covenant signers may or may not be this man.

nehemiah-8:4:3.summary: A Melchia among covenant signers may or may not be this man.

nehemiah-8:4:4.summary: Esam among covenant signers may correspond to Osam here; identity is uncertain.

nehemiah-8:4:5.summary: A Mesoulam among covenant signers may or may not be this man.

nehemiah-8:4:6.summary: The clan of Esam may relate to Osam here; identity is uncertain.

nehemiah-8:4:7.summary: Names a Mesoulam and Phadaia in a Benjamite line; identity with these men is not shown.

nehemiah-8:4:8.summary: A Mesoulam in another list; identity is not shown.

nehemiah-8:4:9.summary: Esabana and Maasaia resemble Asabdana and Maasaia here; identity is uncertain.

nehemiah-8:5:0.summary: Eglon rises when told of “a word from God,” loosely like the people standing for the book.

nehemiah-8:5:1.summary: “The whole assembly of Israel stood” as the king blessed them, a loose parallel.
nehemiah-8:5:1.why: Loose parallel of an assembly standing.

nehemiah-8:5:2.summary: Jesus stands and unrolls the scroll to read publicly, paralleling Esdras opening the book.

nehemiah-8:6:0.summary: Both mention “lifting” hands in prayer, but 1 Timothy gives instruction on church prayer rather than a congregational response to Scripture.
nehemiah-8:6:0.why: Links the gesture of raised hands across both Testaments.

nehemiah-8:6:1.summary: Lamentations calls the people to lift hearts and hands to God, echoing the people’s raised hands in worship.
nehemiah-8:6:1.why: Shows the raised-hands gesture in corporate appeal.

nehemiah-8:6:2.summary: In both the whole people “bowed” and “worshipped” in response to God’s word and visitation.
nehemiah-8:6:2.why: Shows a recurring pattern of corporate worship.

nehemiah-8:6:3.summary: Leader and all the people bow on their faces and worship the Lord together, as in Nehemiah’s assembly.
nehemiah-8:6:3.why: Parallel scene of national prostration in worship.

nehemiah-8:6:4.summary: Heavenly beings fall on their faces and worship God, loosely mirroring the people’s prostration.
nehemiah-8:6:4.why: Earthly worship posture mirrored in heaven.

nehemiah-8:6:5.summary: Abraham’s servant simply “worshipped the Lord”; only the act of worship is shared.

nehemiah-8:6:6.summary: Both join lifting hands with blessing the Lord: “lift your hands … and bless the Lord.”
nehemiah-8:6:6.why: Psalm gives liturgical form of the same act.

nehemiah-8:6:7.summary: Under Nehemiah the whole assembly likewise answered “Amen” and praised the Lord.
nehemiah-8:6:7.why: Same community’s pattern of corporate Amen.

nehemiah-8:6:8.summary: All the people fall on their faces before the Lord, though at the altar fire rather than at a reading.
nehemiah-8:6:8.why: Shared posture of awe before God.

nehemiah-8:6:9.summary: The whole assembly blesses the Lord and prostrates itself at a leader’s call, closely like Esdras’s blessing.
nehemiah-8:6:9.why: Parallel liturgical response of the assembly.

nehemiah-8:6:10.summary: “The people bowed down and worshipped” after hearing God’s instruction, matching the people’s response here.
nehemiah-8:6:10.why: Recurring formula of the people’s worshipful response.

nehemiah-8:6:11.summary: A doxology “Blessed be the Lord God” closing with “May it be!”, akin to blessing followed by Amen.

nehemiah-8:6:12.summary: “Blessed be the Lord, Israel’s God … May it be!” parallels Esdras blessing God and the people’s Amen.
nehemiah-8:6:12.why: Psalm doxology parallels the liturgical form.

nehemiah-8:6:13.summary: The shown Lord’s Prayer verse has no “Amen,” blessing, or worship posture linking it to the source.
nehemiah-8:6:13.why: No real link in the shown text.

nehemiah-8:6:14.summary: “The lifting of my hands” in prayer shares the gesture only.

nehemiah-8:6:15.summary: Opens with “Blessed be the God,” a general echo of blessing God.

nehemiah-8:6:16.summary: Paul assumes hearers “say the Amen” to a blessing they understand, as the people answered Esdras’s blessing.

nehemiah-8:6:17.summary: “Blessed be the God” formula is a general echo of Esdras blessing the Lord.

nehemiah-8:6:18.summary: Solomon’s “Blessed be the Lord, Israel’s God” is a similar leader’s blessing before the assembly.
nehemiah-8:6:18.why: Leader blessing God before the people.

nehemiah-8:6:19.summary: “I lift my hands toward Thy holy temple” shares the raised-hands gesture only.
nehemiah-8:6:19.why: Gesture of prayer toward God’s house.

nehemiah-8:6:20.summary: Abram stretches out his hand to God Most High in an oath, a loose parallel to raised hands.

nehemiah-8:6:21.summary: “I will bless Thee … I will lift my hands” pairs blessing and raised hands as in the source.
nehemiah-8:6:21.why: Same pairing of blessing and lifted hands.

nehemiah-8:6:22.summary: Jesus “fell upon His face and prayed,” sharing only the face-down posture.

nehemiah-8:6:23.summary: In Hezekiah’s restored worship the assembly “fell down, and worshiped” after hymning the Lord.

nehemiah-8:6:24.summary: Jeremiah’s “Truly! May the Lord do so” functions as an Amen, but in a different context.

nehemiah-8:7:0.summary: Names Jesus and Sarabia among the Levites leading the people, the same Levites as in the source.
nehemiah-8:7:0.why: Same Levites lead the people again.

nehemiah-8:7:1.summary: Priests are charged to instruct Israel in the Lord’s statutes, the duty the Levites perform here.
nehemiah-8:7:1.why: Grounds Levitical teaching in the Law.

nehemiah-8:7:2.summary: Lists Levites in a mixed-marriage roll; none of the named Levites (Jesus, Banaias, Sarabia) appears in the shown text.
nehemiah-8:7:2.why: No shared name or event shown.

nehemiah-8:7:3.summary: Wall repairers Benjamin, Asoub and Azaria share no name or activity with the source.

nehemiah-8:7:4.summary: People “seek law” from the priest’s mouth, matching Levites helping the people understand the law.
nehemiah-8:7:4.why: Defines the teaching role of clergy.

nehemiah-8:7:5.summary: Describes the same public reading with Esdras on the platform and his assistants beside him.
nehemiah-8:7:5.why: Immediate context of the same event.

nehemiah-8:7:6.summary: Levites “Jesus son of Azania, of Banaiou” appear in the covenant list, matching Jesus and Banaias.

nehemiah-8:7:8.summary: Names Odouia, Esam, Besi; none matches the Levites in the source.

nehemiah-8:7:9.summary: Saints transliterates “sachol man,” so the “understanding” link the label assumes is absent; no shared names.

nehemiah-8:7:10.summary: Levites and priests go through Judah teaching the people from the book of the Lord’s law.
nehemiah-8:7:10.why: Earlier precedent of Levites teaching the law.

nehemiah-8:7:11.summary: Sarabia and Jesou appear as rulers of the Levites, matching Jesus and Sarabia.

nehemiah-8:7:12.summary: Mentions Levites and Bani, possibly related to Banaias, but in wall repair.

nehemiah-8:7:13.summary: Names Saraia, Azaria and Jermia, priests; none matches the source Levites.

nehemiah-8:7:15.summary: Lists gatekeepers Akoub and Telamin, not named in the source.

nehemiah-8:7:16.summary: Priests with trumpets at the wall dedication share no names with the source.

nehemiah-8:7:17.summary: Praises Levites “who showed good understanding,” loosely echoing Levites giving understanding.

nehemiah-8:7:18.summary: Sarabia appears among Levites sealing the covenant, matching the source’s Sarabia.
nehemiah-8:7:18.why: Same Levite in the covenant roll.

nehemiah-8:7:19.summary: Azour son of Iesous, ruler of Masphe, is a different figure repairing the wall.

nehemiah-8:7:20.summary: Azarias, Esdras and Mesoulam in a procession share no name with the source’s Levites.

nehemiah-8:8:0.summary: Christ opens minds “to understand the Scriptures,” as the people came to understand the reading.

nehemiah-8:8:1.summary: Paul “explained” from the law of Moses to a gathered crowd all day, like Esdras explaining the law.

nehemiah-8:8:2.summary: Paul reasons and explains from the Scriptures, a general parallel to explaining the law.

nehemiah-8:8:3.summary: Writing a vision clearly “so that the one reading” may act loosely parallels clear reading.

nehemiah-8:8:4.summary: Jesus “interpreted” Moses and the prophets, parallel to Esdras explaining the book of the law.

nehemiah-8:8:5.summary: Disciples recall Him opening the Scriptures, a general echo of explained reading.

nehemiah-8:8:6.summary: “Do you understand what you are reading?… unless someone guides me” mirrors explanation enabling understanding.
nehemiah-8:8:6.why: Shows need for a guide to Scripture.

nehemiah-8:8:7.summary: Jesus expounds a commandment of the law, loosely like explaining the law.

nehemiah-8:8:8.summary: Jesus explains the meaning of the adultery commandment, a loose parallel to explaining the law.

nehemiah-8:9:20.summary: Names Neemia and “Esdras the priest and scribe” together, as in the source.

nehemiah-8:9:0.summary: Mentions Neemia receiving gifts, sharing only the person.

nehemiah-8:9:1.summary: Command to “rejoice before the Lord” with the Levite contrasts with weeping on a holy day.

nehemiah-8:9:2.summary: The Saints source names “Neemias,” not “Athersatha,” so the title link assumed by the label is absent.

nehemiah-8:9:3.summary: Esdras the priest brings the law before the assembly, the same reading event.

nehemiah-8:9:4.summary: Command to rejoice before the Lord at the feast loosely supports “do not mourn.”

nehemiah-8:9:5.summary: Mourners receive joy instead of despondency, a general echo of “do not mourn.”

nehemiah-8:9:6.summary: A holy convocation day is decreed, but the date link depends on context not in the source verse.
nehemiah-8:9:6.why: Explains why the day is holy.

nehemiah-8:9:7.summary: “A time to weep and a time to laugh” generally fits the call to stop weeping.
nehemiah-8:9:7.why: Fitting times for sorrow and joy.

nehemiah-8:9:8.summary: Eating and rejoicing before the Lord loosely parallels the call not to mourn.

nehemiah-8:9:9.summary: Command to rejoice in the feast fits the holy day’s joy, but only generally.

nehemiah-8:9:10.summary: Saints source says “Neemias,” not “Athersatha,” so the assumed title link is not carried.

nehemiah-8:9:11.summary: Josiah “heard the words of the law” and grieved, as the people wept hearing the law.
nehemiah-8:9:11.why: Parallel grief at hearing the law.

nehemiah-8:9:12.summary: Names the Levites who helped the people understand, the same group in the source.
nehemiah-8:9:12.why: Immediate context of the same event.

nehemiah-8:9:13.summary: Mentions not eating holy portions in mourning, loosely related to forbidding mourning on a holy day.

nehemiah-8:9:14.summary: Josiah “heard the words of the book of the law” and tore his garments, paralleling the people’s weeping.
nehemiah-8:9:14.why: Parallel grief at hearing the law.

nehemiah-8:9:15.summary: Weeping at the altar is rebuked for hypocrisy; only the word weeping is shared.

nehemiah-8:9:16.summary: Calls Esdras “the priest, the scribe,” the same titles as in the source.

nehemiah-8:9:17.summary: Josiah tells the Levites to minister to the people, a general parallel to Levites serving the people.

nehemiah-8:9:18.summary: Godly sorrow leading to repentance loosely relates to weeping at the law.

nehemiah-8:9:19.summary: When the commandment came, sin came to life—loosely explains grief on hearing the law.

nehemiah-8:9:21.summary: Levites showing understanding and a feast of thanksgiving offer only a general parallel.

nehemiah-8:9:22.summary: Israel without a priest giving guidance or law contrasts with priests and Levites teaching the law.

nehemiah-8:9:23.summary: A holy assembly on the seventh month’s first day; the date is not in the source verse itself.

nehemiah-8:9:24.summary: Josiah fears wrath after the found book’s words, loosely like weeping at the law.

nehemiah-8:9:25.summary: “Through law comes knowledge of sin” loosely explains weeping at the law.

nehemiah-8:9:26.summary: People who forgot God’s law contrast with people now hearing and grieving over it.

nehemiah-8:9:27.summary: Josiah wept before the Lord on hearing His words, as the people wept on hearing the law.
nehemiah-8:9:27.why: Tender response to God’s word honored.

nehemiah-8:9:28.summary: Neemias heads the covenant sealers, the same leader as in the source.

nehemiah-8:10:0.summary: The Lord as helper and stronghold of His people loosely echoes “your strength.”

nehemiah-8:10:1.summary: A rejoicing heart makes one flourish, generally echoing joy as strength.

nehemiah-8:10:2.summary: God’s power in weakness only generally relates to “it is your strength.”

nehemiah-8:10:3.summary: “Eat your bread with gladness and drink your wine” closely echoes “eat … and drink” joyfully.

nehemiah-8:10:4.summary: Joy and strength in the Lord’s salvation loosely echo joy as strength.
nehemiah-8:10:4.why: The Lord as strength and joy.

nehemiah-8:10:5.summary: Rejoicing greatly in the Lord is a general theme match.

nehemiah-8:10:6.summary: Israel rejoicing in its Maker is a general theme match.

nehemiah-8:10:8.summary: Joy overflowing into generosity loosely parallels feasting with portions for the needy.

nehemiah-8:10:10.summary: Eating and drinking as from God’s hand loosely matches the call to feast.

nehemiah-8:10:11.summary: Eating and drinking as God’s gift, a general echo of the festal command.

nehemiah-8:10:12.summary: Encouragement to the fainthearted to be strong loosely echoes “do not lose heart.”

nehemiah-8:10:13.summary: Paul’s confidence in the flesh has no link to the source’s joy, feasting or strength.

nehemiah-8:10:14.summary: “Eat … and drink” as festive invitation shares wording but not context.

nehemiah-8:10:15.summary: Eating and drinking as one’s God-given portion loosely matches the festal command.

nehemiah-8:10:16.summary: Isaiah’s cleansing and commissioning share nothing with the source’s feast or joy.

nehemiah-8:10:17.summary: God provides for enjoyment and the rich should share, loosely echoing feasting and sending portions.

nehemiah-8:10:18.summary: Giving alms loosely parallels sending portions to those who have none.

nehemiah-8:10:19.summary: Job refused to eat “my morsel alone” without sharing with the orphan, like sending portions to those without.

nehemiah-8:10:20.summary: “Give a share to seven” parallels sending portions to others.

nehemiah-8:10:21.summary: Zion is told to rejoice in the Lord who gave food, a general echo of festive eating and joy.

nehemiah-8:10:22.summary: Rejoicing in God’s gifts while giving food to Levite, orphan and widow parallels feasting and sending portions to the needy.
nehemiah-8:10:22.why: Law behind festal sharing with the poor.

nehemiah-8:10:23.summary: People “make merry, and will send gifts to one another,” echoing festive portion-sending in a perverse context.

nehemiah-8:12:0.summary: Love of God’s law as meditation, only generally related to rejoicing over understood words.

nehemiah-8:12:1.summary: Hearts burning as Scripture is opened loosely parallels gladness from understood words.

nehemiah-8:12:2.summary: “The disclosure of Thy words will give … understanding,” as the words made known gave understanding.

nehemiah-8:12:3.summary: Valuing God’s law above riches, a general theme of delight in the law.

nehemiah-8:12:4.summary: Praise flows when God teaches His ordinances, loosely like celebration after teaching.

nehemiah-8:12:5.summary: God’s testimonies are “my heart’s rejoicing,” matching gladness because the words were understood.

nehemiah-8:12:6.summary: Love for the law and meditation on it is a general theme link.

nehemiah-8:12:7.summary: Sweetness of God’s sayings and understanding from commandments loosely match joy in understood words.

nehemiah-8:12:8.summary: Love of God’s commandments above gold, a general theme only.

nehemiah-8:12:9.summary: Describes how the people came to understand the reading, the cause of the gladness in the source.

nehemiah-8:12:10.summary: Meditating on and not forgetting God’s words is a general theme only.

nehemiah-8:12:11.summary: Treasuring God’s words in one’s breast is a general theme only.

nehemiah-8:12:12.summary: The Lord’s ordinances are “rejoicing the heart,” matching joy that follows understanding the law.

nehemiah-8:12:13.summary: Delighting in God’s testimonies as wealth is a general theme link.

nehemiah-8:12:14.summary: Wisdom entering the mind and seeming good is a loose parallel to understanding bringing joy.

nehemiah-8:12:15.summary: Paul’s inability to do good has no link to celebration after understanding the law.

nehemiah-8:12:16.summary: Joy of returned captives is a general theme; it does not concern understanding God’s words.

nehemiah-8:12:17.summary: Honey’s sweetness as an image of wisdom only loosely relates to joy in understanding.

nehemiah-8:12:18.summary: “Thy word will become to me rejoicing and my heart’s joy,” matching gladness over understood words.

nehemiah-8:13:0.summary: Applying the heart to understanding God’s commands loosely parallels attending to the law’s words.

nehemiah-8:13:1.summary: Loving discipline versus hating rebuke has no specific link to gathering to study the law.

nehemiah-8:13:2.summary: Blessing on one who listens daily at wisdom’s doors loosely echoes gathering to attend to the law.

nehemiah-8:13:3.summary: A crowd gathers and Jesus teaches them, a general parallel to gathering around a teacher.

nehemiah-8:13:4.summary: The preceding day’s reading and explanation by Esdras and the Levites, continued in the source.

nehemiah-8:13:5.summary: People “hung on His words,” loosely like leaders attending to the law’s words.

nehemiah-8:13:6.summary: Assembly extends the feast another seven days; only a general parallel of continued observance.

nehemiah-8:13:7.summary: A servant of the Lord must be “able to teach,” a general link to Esdras teaching.

nehemiah-8:13:8.summary: Scriptures opened to disciples loosely parallels gathering to understand the law.

nehemiah-8:13:9.summary: Priests confronting apostles share only the word “priests” with the source.

nehemiah-8:13:10.summary: People ask to hear the words again next Sabbath, loosely like returning the second day for more.

nehemiah-8:14:0.summary: The law commands the “Feast of Tents” in the “seventh month,” exactly what they found written.

nehemiah-8:14:3.summary: Nations will go up yearly to celebrate the “Festival of Tent-Pitching,” the same feast.
nehemiah-8:14:3.why: Future universal keeping of the feast.

nehemiah-8:14:4.summary: Jacob makes booths at a place named Booths; only the word links them.

nehemiah-8:14:5.summary: Names the “feast of Booths,” the same feast of tents described in the source.

nehemiah-8:15:1.summary: Feasts to be proclaimed at their times loosely parallels signaling the feast.

nehemiah-8:15:2.summary: Lists the “Feast of the Pitching of Tents” among pilgrim feasts, a general link.

nehemiah-8:15:3.summary: Abimelech’s men cut wood on a mountain to burn a tower; only going to a hill to cut branches is shared.

nehemiah-8:15:4.summary: Shares only the olive leaf; the dove’s sprig has no festal context.

nehemiah-8:15:5.summary: Mention of the Mount of Olives is incidental to gathering olive leaves in the hill country.

nehemiah-8:15:6.summary: Crowds take palm branches for a festal welcome, echoing palms in festival use.

nehemiah-8:15:7.summary: Heavenly multitude holds palm branches, loosely echoing festal palms.

nehemiah-8:16:0.summary: Names the Ephraim Gate of Jerusalem, the same landmark in the source.

nehemiah-8:16:2.summary: Mentions the Water Gate, which does not appear in the Saints source verse.

nehemiah-8:16:3.summary: Water Gate reference is absent from the Saints source, which names only the Ephraim Gate.

nehemiah-8:16:4.summary: Roofs used for Baal worship share only the word “roofs” with the festal tents.

nehemiah-8:16:5.summary: The public law reading in the same festival setting, but no place named in common.

nehemiah-8:16:6.summary: Mentions the courtyard of the Lord’s house, a place where tents were built.

nehemiah-8:16:7.summary: The temple’s courtyards were once used for idolatrous altars, contrasting with festal tents there.

nehemiah-8:16:8.summary: David on his roof shares only the word “roof.”

nehemiah-8:16:9.summary: Idolatrous incense on roofs shares only the word “roofs.”

nehemiah-8:16:10.summary: Roof parapets imply usable flat roofs, background for tents on roofs.

nehemiah-8:16:11.summary: The people gathered in an open space in the city, similar to the squares where tents were pitched.

nehemiah-8:17:0.summary: Lists the Feast of Tents among Solomon’s offerings, a general link to the feast.

nehemiah-8:17:2.summary: Solomon’s seventh-month seven-day feast with a great assembly ended in rejoicing, like this great gladness.

nehemiah-8:17:3.summary: “Great rejoicing” and “since the days of Solomon” no such festival, matching the source’s unprecedented-since formula.

nehemiah-8:17:4.summary: A seven-day feast kept with great rejoicing is a general parallel.

nehemiah-8:17:5.summary: Mentions Joshua, the same figure as “Jesus son of Naue,” but on a different point.

nehemiah-8:17:6.summary: Patriarchs as sojourners loosely relates to living in tents.

nehemiah-8:17:7.summary: “No Passover like it … since the days of Samuel” parallels a feast unmatched since Joshua’s days.

nehemiah-8:17:8.summary: Eating and drinking before the Lord “with joy” is a general festal parallel.

nehemiah-8:17:9.summary: Saints’ “dwelt among us” does not show the tent wording the label assumes.

nehemiah-8:17:10.summary: Abraham dwelling “in tents” as a foreigner loosely echoes living in tents.

nehemiah-8:17:11.summary: Introduces Joshua son of Nun, the same leader the source calls “Jesus son of Naue.”

nehemiah-8:18:1.summary: “On the eighth day you shall hold a closing festival,” the ordinance followed in the source.

nehemiah-8:18:3.summary: “The last day, the great day of the feast” is the same feast’s climax, where Jesus speaks.

nehemiah-9:1:0.summary: Ezra’s company fasted and sought God, a general parallel to fasting.

nehemiah-9:1:6.summary: Solomon dismissed the people on the twenty-third of the seventh month, a near date parallel.

nehemiah-9:1:8.summary: Torn garments and earth on head are absent from the Saints source verse.

nehemiah-9:1:13.summary: Jews mourning in “sackcloth” corporately, paralleling Israel’s sackcloth.
