nehemiah-9:1:16.summary: “Sackcloth,” “Consecrate a fast,” and gathering the land’s inhabitants parallel the source’s assembly.

nehemiah-9:1:17.summary: Nineveh “proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth,” the same pair of penitential acts.

nehemiah-9:1:18.summary: “They fasted that day, put on sackcloth,” closely matching the source.

nehemiah-9:1:19.summary: Sackcloth worn in supplication, but no fast or assembly for confession.

nehemiah-9:2:0.summary: Upon hearing the law, the mixed population “was separated,” as Israel separated from foreigners.
nehemiah-9:2:0.why: Same separation at a later reading.

nehemiah-9:2:1.summary: Daniel, with fasts and sackcloth, confesses the sins of the people, kings and fathers.

nehemiah-9:2:2.summary: Esdras commands, “Separate yourselves from the peoples of the land,” the act Israel performs here.
nehemiah-9:2:2.why: Earlier call to the same separation.

nehemiah-9:2:3.summary: Nehemiah “purified them from all foreign association,” matching separation from every foreigner.

nehemiah-9:2:4.summary: Daniel confesses “my sins and the sins of my people,” like Israel confessing its own and its fathers’ sins.

nehemiah-9:2:5.summary: The “holy seed” mixed with the peoples of the lands explains why Israel separated from foreigners.

nehemiah-9:2:6.summary: “Foreign children” born to unfaithful Israel loosely relates to separating from foreigners.

nehemiah-9:2:7.summary: “If we confess our sins” is a general theme of confession.

nehemiah-9:2:8.summary: A plea for rescue from foreigners’ hands shares only the word foreigners.

nehemiah-9:2:9.summary: Rescue “from the hand of foreigners” is unrelated to separating and confessing.

nehemiah-9:2:10.summary: Nehemiah “confess[es] concerning the sins of the sons of Israel … I and my father’s house have sinned.”
nehemiah-9:2:10.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

nehemiah-9:2:11.summary: Esdras confesses “our lawless deeds” since “the days of our fathers,” as the people confess their fathers’ lawless deeds.

nehemiah-9:2:12.summary: Israel filled with foreign ways and foreign children loosely relates to separation from foreigners.
nehemiah-9:2:12.why: Foreign influence as cause of judgment.

nehemiah-9:2:14.summary: Esdras admits “we are before Thee in our offenses,” a general confession parallel.

nehemiah-9:2:15.summary: “We sinned with our fathers; we acted lawlessly,” echoing confession of sins and fathers’ lawless deeds.

nehemiah-9:3:1.summary: The earlier public reading from the book of the law with the people attentive parallels this reading.
nehemiah-9:3:1.why: Earlier reading of the same law.

nehemiah-9:4:0.summary: Jesus and Sarabia appear as Levites helping the people, the same Levites as here.

nehemiah-9:4:1.summary: The Levites Jesus and Kadmiel lead the people in blessing, continuing the same scene.

nehemiah-9:4:2.summary: Jesus, Kadmiel and Sarabia appear among the Levites sealing the covenant.
nehemiah-9:4:2.why: Same Levites in the covenant roll.

nehemiah-9:4:3.summary: Lists Levites Jesou, Kadmiel and Sarabia, matching the source names.

nehemiah-9:4:5.summary: Jesus crying “with a loud voice” to Lazarus shares only the phrase.

nehemiah-9:4:6.summary: Stephen “cried with a loud voice” to the Lord in prayer, a loose verbal echo.

nehemiah-9:4:7.summary: Crying out to God in prayer is a general parallel.

nehemiah-9:4:8.summary: “With my voice I cried to the Lord” is a general echo of crying out.

nehemiah-9:4:9.summary: “With my voice I cried to the Lord” is a general echo.

nehemiah-9:4:10.summary: Crying to the Lord from the depths; “ascents” refers to a song title, not the Levites’ ascent.

nehemiah-9:5:0.summary: “Bless the Lord … His holy name” matches the call to bless the Lord and His glorious name.

nehemiah-9:5:1.summary: “Blessed be the God” is a general doxological parallel.

nehemiah-9:5:2.summary: Light of the knowledge of God’s glory has no specific link to the call to bless God.

nehemiah-9:5:3.summary: Jesus’ thanksgiving for revelation to infants has no specific link to the Levites’ summons.

nehemiah-9:5:4.summary: Asking who can make all God’s praises heard loosely echoes His name being above all praise.

nehemiah-9:5:6.summary: “Blessed be His glorious name for the age” closely matches blessing His glorious name forever.

nehemiah-9:5:7.summary: Call to praise the Lord is a general theme only.

nehemiah-9:5:8.summary: Restored exiles giving thanks to the Lord is a general parallel.

nehemiah-9:5:9.summary: Returned exiles praise the Lord at the temple’s founding, a general parallel.

nehemiah-9:5:10.summary: Levites “stood up to praise the Lord” with a loud voice, matching Levites calling the people to stand and bless.

nehemiah-9:5:11.summary: Glory to God for all generations loosely echoes everlasting blessing.

nehemiah-9:5:12.summary: God exceeds heaven and heaven of heaven, loosely like His name exalted above all praise.

nehemiah-9:5:13.summary: Speaking of the glory of God’s holiness is a general praise theme.

nehemiah-9:5:14.summary: Solomon stands before the assembly to pray; only the standing assembly setting is shared.

nehemiah-9:5:15.summary: Lifelong praise of God is a general theme only.

nehemiah-9:5:16.summary: God glorified beyond all gods loosely echoes exaltation above all praise.

nehemiah-9:5:17.summary: “I will bless Thee and praise Thy name for the age and for the age of the age” matches everlasting blessing of His name.

nehemiah-9:5:18.summary: All Judah “stood before the Lord,” loosely like the call to stand up.

nehemiah-9:5:19.summary: Praise of the Lord’s glorified right hand is a general praise parallel.

nehemiah-9:5:20.summary: God needs nothing from us, loosely echoing a name above all blessing.

nehemiah-9:5:21.summary: God’s “honoured and wondrous name” loosely echoes His glorious name.

nehemiah-9:5:22.summary: Speaking of the glory of God’s kingdom is a general praise theme.

nehemiah-9:5:23.summary: The assembly stood while the king blessed, loosely like standing to bless.

nehemiah-9:5:24.summary: David’s call “Bless the Lord your God” is the same summons the Levites give.

nehemiah-9:5:26.summary: “Bless the Lord, all slaves of the Lord, who stand,” matching the call to stand and bless.

nehemiah-9:5:27.summary: Exalt the Lord as much as you can, “for He will surpass even that,” like a name above all praise.

nehemiah-9:6:0.summary: “Thou alone art God … Thou didst make heaven and earth” closely matches Esdras’s opening confession.

nehemiah-9:6:1.summary: “God made heaven and earth,” the creation event Esdras’s prayer recalls.

nehemiah-9:6:2.summary: Heaven worships God because “Thou didst create all things,” matching creation and heavenly worship.

nehemiah-9:6:3.summary: “Heaven and the heaven of heaven, the earth and all that is therein” closely matches the source.

nehemiah-9:6:4.summary: “The Lord is one” underlies “Thou alone art the Lord.”

nehemiah-9:6:5.summary: “Heaven and earth … and all their ordered array” echoes heaven and “all their array.”

nehemiah-9:6:6.summary: No God apart from Me is a general monotheistic parallel.

nehemiah-9:6:7.summary: “Thou alone art God … Thou madest heaven and earth” closely matches the source.

nehemiah-9:6:8.summary: “Apart from Me there is no God” loosely matches “Thou alone art the Lord.”

nehemiah-9:6:9.summary: The Lord who made earth and heaven versus gods who did not, matching sole Creator confession.

nehemiah-9:6:10.summary: No god before or after Me, a general monotheistic theme.

nehemiah-9:6:11.summary: “Thou alone art the great God” closely echoes “Thou alone art the Lord.”

nehemiah-9:6:12.summary: Worship “the One who made heaven and the earth and sea,” matching Creator of heaven, earth and seas.

nehemiah-9:6:13.summary: Angels and every creature in heaven, earth and sea worship God, like heaven’s armies worshiping.

nehemiah-9:6:14.summary: Shares the phrase “heaven of heaven” but in a temple-dedication context.

nehemiah-9:6:15.summary: The Lord saves humans and beasts, loosely like giving life to all things.

nehemiah-9:6:16.summary: All things in heaven and on earth created through Him and held together, paralleling creation and preservation.

nehemiah-9:6:17.summary: “Upholding all things” loosely echoes giving life to all things.

nehemiah-9:6:18.summary: Seraphim worship the Lord, loosely like heaven’s armies worshiping.

nehemiah-9:6:19.summary: “Thou alone art God” matches the source’s confession of God’s uniqueness.

nehemiah-9:6:20.summary: “Thou art the Lord, God alone” closely matches “Thou alone art the Lord.”

nehemiah-9:6:21.summary: Jesus cites “the Lord is one,” a general monotheistic parallel.

nehemiah-9:6:23.summary: Praise to Him who made the heavens, earth and lights, a parallel creation litany.

nehemiah-9:6:24.summary: All God’s angels worship the Son, loosely like heaven’s armies worshiping.

nehemiah-9:6:25.summary: “Made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them” closely matches the source.

nehemiah-9:6:26.summary: Commands by which a person lives share only the idea of life, not creation.

nehemiah-9:6:27.summary: The heavens and “all their power” established by God’s word, like heaven and all their array.

nehemiah-9:6:28.summary: “All the army of heaven stood around Him,” matching the armies of heaven before God.

nehemiah-9:6:29.summary: “Bless the Lord, all His powers,” calling heavenly hosts to worship as the source describes.

nehemiah-9:6:30.summary: “I and the Father are one” does not carry the source’s sole-Creator confession.

nehemiah-9:6:31.summary: Jacob sees “the camp of God,” loosely relating to heavenly armies.

nehemiah-9:6:32.summary: Prayer to the “Creator of all … the only King” parallels the sole-Creator confession.

nehemiah-9:7:0.summary: Abram is led “out of the country of the Chaldeans,” the same phrase as the source.

nehemiah-9:7:2.summary: God “called him” and blessed Abraham, matching God choosing Abram.

nehemiah-9:7:3.summary: Stephen recounts God calling Abraham, who “left the land of the Chaldeans.”

nehemiah-9:7:4.summary: God chose Israel, “offspring of Abraham,” echoing God’s choice of Abram.

nehemiah-9:7:5.summary: God calls Abram out and promises to “make your name great,” the call recounted here.

nehemiah-9:7:6.summary: The Lord chose the fathers and their seed, echoing God choosing Abram.

nehemiah-9:7:8.summary: “I took your father Abraham from beyond the River,” a parallel historical recital.
nehemiah-9:7:8.why: Earlier recital of the same history.

nehemiah-9:8:1.summary: God cannot lie, loosely echoing God fulfilling His words because He is righteous.

nehemiah-9:8:3.summary: “Not one word has failed” of the Lord’s promises, matching “Thou didst fulfil Thy words.”

nehemiah-9:8:4.summary: “To your seed I will give this land,” the promise referenced in the source.

nehemiah-9:8:5.summary: God establishes His covenant to give Abram’s seed “all the land of Canaan.”

nehemiah-9:8:6.summary: God “who does not lie” keeps His promise, a general echo of God fulfilling His words.

nehemiah-9:8:7.summary: The Lord gave Israel the land sworn to their fathers; “not one of all the good words … failed.”

nehemiah-9:8:8.summary: Lists Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Girgashites and Jebusites as the promised land’s peoples.

nehemiah-9:8:9.summary: God is “faithful and just,” a general echo of God being righteous.

nehemiah-9:8:10.summary: Abraham’s faith was proven and “reckoned to him as righteousness,” matching his heart found faithful.

nehemiah-9:8:11.summary: “Having spoken, shall He not act?” parallels God fulfilling His words.

nehemiah-9:8:12.summary: God “found David … a man after My heart,” a loose echo of finding Abram’s heart faithful.

nehemiah-9:8:13.summary: After Abraham’s obedience God swears to bless his seed and give them enemies’ cities.

nehemiah-9:8:14.summary: Abraham, tested, offered Isaac by faith, a general echo of his faithful heart.

nehemiah-9:8:15.summary: God “gave them countries of nations,” the fulfilment of the land promise.

nehemiah-9:8:16.summary: Lists several of the same Canaanite peoples, but in a battle context.

nehemiah-9:8:17.summary: Declaring that the Lord is upright loosely echoes “Thou art righteous.”

nehemiah-9:8:18.summary: Christ “considered me faithful,” a loose verbal echo of finding Abram faithful.

nehemiah-9:8:19.summary: God remembered the covenant “He covenanted with Abraham,” the covenant recalled here.

nehemiah-9:8:20.summary: The Lord “kept the oath which He sware unto your fathers” and is “the faithful God.”
nehemiah-9:8:20.why: God’s faithfulness to the patriarchal oath.

nehemiah-9:8:21.summary: Joshua took all the land, a general fulfilment of the land promise.

nehemiah-9:8:22.summary: Lists Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites and Jebusites, the same peoples named in the source.

nehemiah-9:8:23.summary: God gives the land to “establish His covenant which He sware unto your fathers, Abraham.”
nehemiah-9:8:23.why: Land given to keep the covenant.

nehemiah-9:8:24.summary: Abram’s call and promise of blessing, but without the land covenant and nations named here.

nehemiah-9:8:25.summary: Lists the same Canaanite nations, but as kings reacting to Joshua.

nehemiah-9:8:26.summary: “Now I know that you fear God” is God finding Abraham’s heart faithful.

nehemiah-9:8:27.summary: God remembers “His holy covenant, the oath He swore to Abraham,” fulfilled in Christ.

nehemiah-9:8:28.summary: Promises the place of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Girgashites and Jebusites.

nehemiah-9:8:29.summary: Israel declares it has come into “the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers,” confessing fulfilment.

nehemiah-9:8:30.summary: Abraham “entered a covenant” and “was found faithful,” closely matching the source.

nehemiah-9:9:1.summary: “I have indeed seen the mistreatment of My people in Egypt and heard their groaning.”

nehemiah-9:9:3.summary: God has “seen all that has befallen you in Egypt,” matching seeing their humiliation.

nehemiah-9:9:4.summary: “God looked upon the sons of Israel” in Egypt, matching God seeing their humiliation.

nehemiah-9:10:0.summary: “Signs … in Egypt … and madest a name for Thyself as it is this day” is nearly identical.

nehemiah-9:10:1.summary: God brought His people out of Egypt and “didst make Thyself a name as on this day.”

nehemiah-9:10:2.summary: God overpowered water “to make Himself an everlasting name” at the Exodus.

nehemiah-9:10:3.summary: God is glorified “through Pharaoh and all his army” at the sea, the events summarized here.

nehemiah-9:10:4.summary: Pharaoh’s defiant “Who is He, that I should obey” shows the arrogance the source mentions.

nehemiah-9:10:5.summary: God led His people “to make Thyself a glorious name,” a general echo.

nehemiah-9:10:6.summary: God took a nation “by signs, and by wonders” in Egypt, matching signs performed in Egypt.

nehemiah-9:10:7.summary: Saints reads “because they attacked them,” not arrogance, so the link is only general.

nehemiah-9:10:8.summary: “He set His signs in Egypt” and lists the plagues, the signs the source recalls.

nehemiah-9:10:10.summary: Through Pharaoh God demonstrated power “so that My name might be proclaimed,” matching making a name.

nehemiah-9:10:11.summary: Let them know “Thy name is Lord,” a general echo of God’s name.

nehemiah-9:10:12.summary: Belshazzar’s sacrilege is a different arrogant king; no Egypt or signs link.

nehemiah-9:10:13.summary: God saved them at the Red Sea “for His name’s sake, to make His might known.”

nehemiah-9:10:14.summary: Rahab heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea, showing the name God made spreading.

nehemiah-9:10:15.summary: Pharaoh’s harsh brick orders illustrate Egyptian oppression only generally.

nehemiah-9:10:16.summary: Praise to Him who struck Egypt and shook “Pharaoh and his force into the Red Sea.”

nehemiah-9:10:17.summary: “Signs and wonders … upon Pharaoh and all his slaves” closely matches signs against Pharao and his servants.

nehemiah-9:10:18.summary: God acted in bringing Israel out of Egypt for His name before the nations.

nehemiah-9:10:19.summary: “Signs and His wonders … unto Pharaoh king of Egypt and unto all his land” matches the source.

nehemiah-9:10:20.summary: Moses did “wonders and signs in the land of Egypt,” as recalled here.

nehemiah-9:10:21.summary: “God opposes the proud” loosely relates to God acting against arrogant Egypt.

nehemiah-9:10:22.summary: The wonders “in Egypt’s land” before their fathers, matching signs in Egypt.

nehemiah-9:10:23.summary: God humbles the insolent and arrogant, a general parallel to judging arrogant Egypt.

nehemiah-9:10:24.summary: “His signs and portents in the land of Ham” lists the plagues the source summarizes.

nehemiah-9:10:25.summary: God “performs signs and wonders,” a general parallel to signs in Egypt.

nehemiah-9:11:0.summary: “He tore the sea apart and led them through,” matching breaking open the sea.

nehemiah-9:11:3.summary: “The sea saw and fled,” a poetic image of the sea opening before Israel.

nehemiah-9:11:4.summary: God overpowered water and “led them through the abyss,” recalling the sea crossing.

nehemiah-9:11:5.summary: God divided the Red Sea, led Israel through, and shook Pharaoh’s force into it.

nehemiah-9:11:6.summary: He “turns the sea into dry land” so they pass on foot, matching crossing on dry ground.

nehemiah-9:11:7.summary: They “crossed the Red Sea as through dry land” while the Egyptians were swallowed.

nehemiah-9:11:8.summary: God dried the Red Sea, guided them through the deep, and water covered their enemies.

nehemiah-9:11:9.summary: A stone hurled into the sea pictures sudden destruction, the same image used for Egypt’s pursuers.

nehemiah-9:12:1.summary: Repeats pillar of cloud by day and fire by night “to light for them the way they should travel.”

nehemiah-9:12:3.summary: God “guided them with a cloud by day, and all night with the light of fire.”

nehemiah-9:12:6.summary: God spread a cloud and “fire to light the night for them.”

nehemiah-9:12:2.summary: The “pillar of cloud” moves to protect Israel in the Exodus narrative.

nehemiah-9:12:4.summary: Prayer to know “the way I shall walk” is a general guidance theme.

nehemiah-9:12:5.summary: God “guided them into a straight way to travel,” a general guidance parallel.

nehemiah-9:12:7.summary: God supplied “a fire-blazing pillar, a guide for an unknown journey,” the same pillar of fire.

nehemiah-9:13:0.summary: God’s words are “truth” and His judgments righteous, a general echo of laws of truth.

nehemiah-9:13:1.summary: “The Lord spoke all these words,” the Sinai giving of the law recalled here.

nehemiah-9:13:2.summary: Love for God’s commandments is a general theme only.

nehemiah-9:13:3.summary: “The Lord will come down on Mount Sinai,” matching “Thou camest down upon Mount Sina.”

nehemiah-9:13:4.summary: “The commandment holy and righteous and good” matches good ordinances and upright judgments.

nehemiah-9:13:5.summary: “The Lord’s ordinances are upright … the Lord’s judgments are true,” matching the source’s descriptions.

nehemiah-9:13:6.summary: The Lord spoke these words to the assembly “on the mountain, out of the midst of the fire.”

nehemiah-9:13:7.summary: God “gave them My commands and made My ordinances known,” as at Sinai.

nehemiah-9:13:8.summary: No nation has “ordinances and judgments as righteous as all this law,” matching upright judgments.

nehemiah-9:13:9.summary: Israel heard God’s voice speaking out of the fire, as God spoke to them.

nehemiah-9:13:10.summary: God opening heaven and mountains trembling loosely echoes God descending on Sinai.

nehemiah-9:13:12.summary: “The Lord spoke with you … on the mountain,” matching God speaking at Sinai.

nehemiah-9:13:14.summary: “Thy judgment is upright” echoes upright judgments only generally.

nehemiah-9:13:15.summary: Mountains tremble when God acts, a loose theophany echo.

nehemiah-9:13:16.summary: Agreement that the law is good is a general echo of good ordinances.

nehemiah-9:13:17.summary: God coming from a mountain is a general theophany parallel.

nehemiah-9:13:18.summary: At Horeb the Lord spoke “out of the midst of the fire” and declared His covenant.

nehemiah-9:13:19.summary: Keeping God’s commandments and ordinances is a general theme only.

nehemiah-9:13:20.summary: “The Lord has come from Sinai,” matching God coming down on Sina.

nehemiah-9:13:21.summary: Recalls the Sinai mountain with fire, darkness and “a voice speaking words,” contrasting it with Zion.

nehemiah-9:14:1.summary: God gave Israel His “sabbaths” as a sign in the wilderness, matching Nehemiah’s confession that He made His holy Sabbath known.
nehemiah-9:14:1.why: Shows the Sabbath as covenant sign given at the Exodus.

nehemiah-9:14:2.summary: God blessed and hallowed the seventh day; background to the “holy Sabbath” but not about its revelation to Israel.
nehemiah-9:14:2.why: Roots the holy Sabbath in creation.

nehemiah-9:14:3.summary: God tells Israel to sanctify “My sabbaths” as a sign, echoing the Sabbath made known to them.
nehemiah-9:14:3.why: Explains the Sabbath’s purpose as covenant sign.

nehemiah-9:14:4.summary: Moses first announces “a holy rest to the Lord” in the manna episode, the moment the holy Sabbath was made known.
nehemiah-9:14:4.why: Narrative of the Sabbath’s first disclosure to Israel.

nehemiah-9:14:5.summary: “The Lord has given you this day, the Sabbath” in the wilderness, the event Nehemiah recalls.
nehemiah-9:14:5.why: Shows the Sabbath given as gift in the wilderness.

nehemiah-9:14:6.summary: Summary of “commandments that the Lord commanded Moses” at Sinai, matching commandments given through Moses.
nehemiah-9:14:6.why: Locates the commandments’ giving at Sinai.

nehemiah-9:14:7.summary: Nehemiah recalls the word God “didst command Moses Thy servant”, a verbal echo but about scattering, not the Sinai laws.

nehemiah-9:14:8.summary: God speaks to Moses “the commandments, and the ordinances, and the judgments” to teach Israel, the same triad.
nehemiah-9:14:8.why: Shows Moses as mediator of the law.

nehemiah-9:14:9.summary: Moses has shown Israel “ordinances and judgments” as the Lord commanded; a general parallel to law given through Moses.
nehemiah-9:14:9.why: Moses as teacher of the law.

nehemiah-9:14:10.summary: “The testimonies, and the ordinances, and the judgments which Moses spoke” to Israel after the Exodus.
nehemiah-9:14:10.why: Parallel summary of law given through Moses.

nehemiah-9:14:11.summary: “The Law was given through Moses” directly echoes law commanded “through Moses”.
nehemiah-9:14:11.why: Contrasts Mosaic law with grace through Christ.

nehemiah-9:14:12.summary: Opens “the ordinances which you shall set before them”, an example of Mosaic ordinances; shown text is slave law only (truncated).
nehemiah-9:14:12.why: Sample of the ordinances given at Sinai.

nehemiah-9:15:0.summary: Paul recalls Israel’s “spiritual food” and drink from the “rock”, the same wilderness bread and water.

nehemiah-9:15:4.summary: Narrative of the manna: “This is the bread the Lord has given you to eat.”
nehemiah-9:15:4.why: The original account of bread from heaven.

nehemiah-9:15:5.summary: “He gave them bread from heaven to eat” is quoted and applied by Jesus to Himself as true bread.
nehemiah-9:15:5.why: Shows manna fulfilled in Christ, the bread of life.

nehemiah-9:15:6.summary: Psalm recalls “bread from heaven” and a split rock pouring waters, both gifts named in Nehemiah.
nehemiah-9:15:6.why: Parallel liturgical recital of wilderness provision.

nehemiah-9:15:7.summary: God raised His hand that the rebels would not enter the land, contrasting the land He swore to give.
nehemiah-9:15:7.why: Shows the oath reversed by disobedience.

nehemiah-9:15:8.summary: God “fed you with manna” in the wilderness, teaching dependence on His word.
nehemiah-9:15:8.why: Explains the purpose of the bread from heaven.

nehemiah-9:15:9.summary: God “turned the rock into pools of water”, recalling water from a rock.
nehemiah-9:15:9.why: Poetic praise of the same miracle.

nehemiah-9:15:10.summary: He “rained manna” and gave “heaven’s bread”, the same bread from heaven.
nehemiah-9:15:10.why: Parallel recital of the manna gift.

nehemiah-9:15:11.summary: Recalls Exodus redemption and guidance by Moses and Aaron, but not bread or water from the rock.

nehemiah-9:15:12.summary: Same prayer repeats manna “from their mouths” and “water for their thirst”.

nehemiah-9:15:13.summary: The land “over which I stretched out My hand” to settle them, the same oath idiom for the land.
nehemiah-9:15:13.why: Shows the sworn land and its forfeiture.

nehemiah-9:15:14.summary: Moses brings “water out of the rock” for the congregation at Meribah.
nehemiah-9:15:14.why: Narrative of water from the rock.

nehemiah-9:15:15.summary: God commands entry into “the land that I am giving them”, echoing the call to enter and inherit.
nehemiah-9:15:15.why: Shows fulfillment of the land command under Joshua.

nehemiah-9:15:16.summary: Abram’s oath gesture “stretch out my hand” only shares the idiom; no link to wilderness provision or the land gift.

nehemiah-9:15:17.summary: God brought “a spring of water out of the sheer rock” and “fed you with manna”, both gifts listed.

nehemiah-9:15:18.summary: “Go up and inherit it” matches God telling them to enter and inherit the land.
nehemiah-9:15:18.why: The original command to possess the land.

nehemiah-9:15:19.summary: God supplied “ready bread from heaven” and angels’ food to His people.

nehemiah-9:16:0.summary: Same prayer: they “stiffened their necks and did not listen” to God’s commandments.

nehemiah-9:16:1.summary: “My people did not listen to My voice”, God’s lament over Israel’s refusal.
nehemiah-9:16:1.why: God’s own voice on the same disobedience.

nehemiah-9:16:2.summary: “Hardness and unrepentant heart” storing up wrath; general theme of stubbornness.

nehemiah-9:16:3.summary: Moses names Israel’s “stiff neck” and provocation, the same charge.
nehemiah-9:16:3.why: Moses’ testimony to the fathers’ stubbornness.

nehemiah-9:16:4.summary: “Do not harden your hearts as in the provocation”; general warning based on wilderness rebellion.
nehemiah-9:16:4.why: Applies the fathers’ failure to believers.

nehemiah-9:16:5.summary: Egyptians “acted arrogantly” against Israel; now Israel’s fathers “acted arrogantly” against God.
nehemiah-9:16:5.why: Ironic reversal within the same prayer.

nehemiah-9:16:6.summary: The wilderness generation hardened hearts and tested God, “they did not know My ways”.
nehemiah-9:16:6.why: Psalm parallel to the fathers’ rebellion.

nehemiah-9:16:7.summary: “If you had listened to My commands”; general lament over not heeding commandments.
nehemiah-9:16:7.why: Shows what obedience would have brought.

nehemiah-9:16:8.summary: Exhortation that none be “hardened”; general theme only.

nehemiah-9:16:9.summary: Jacob grew fat and “forsook God”; rebellion theme without shared wording.
nehemiah-9:16:9.why: Song of Moses on Israel’s ingratitude.

nehemiah-9:16:10.summary: “They hardened their necks so as not to listen to My words”, nearly identical phrasing.

nehemiah-9:16:11.summary: God testifies “if you listen to Me”; appeal to hear, general theme.

nehemiah-9:16:12.summary: Israel “disobeyed the word of the Lord” and refused to go up at Kadesh, a concrete instance of the fathers’ refusal.

nehemiah-9:16:13.summary: “Your neck an iron sinew”; stubbornness image, addressed to a later generation.
nehemiah-9:16:13.why: Vivid image of a stiff neck.

nehemiah-9:16:14.summary: Moses: they “did not hearken unto His voice” and were disobedient from the start.
nehemiah-9:16:14.why: Moses’ summary of the fathers’ disobedience.

nehemiah-9:16:15.summary: God calls Israel “a stiff-necked people” at the calf episode.
nehemiah-9:16:15.why: Divine verdict on the same generation.

nehemiah-9:16:16.summary: People saying “we will come to Thee no more”; general rejection theme.

nehemiah-9:16:18.summary: Zedekiah “hardened his neck”; same idiom but a different person and era.
nehemiah-9:16:18.why: Shows the idiom recurring in later kings.

nehemiah-9:16:19.summary: God longs that they would “keep My commandments”; general obedience theme.

nehemiah-9:16:20.summary: Promise if Israel would “give ear to His commandments”; general theme.

nehemiah-9:16:21.summary: Psalm recounts the fathers as a “crooked and embittering generation” who did not keep God’s covenant or law.
nehemiah-9:16:21.why: Extended psalm recital of the same history.

nehemiah-9:16:22.summary: “They did not listen. They hardened their back more than the back of their fathers.”

nehemiah-9:16:23.summary: “We sinned with our fathers” mirrors confession of the fathers’ sin.

nehemiah-9:16:24.summary: “They disobeyed and provoked His holy spirit”; general rebellion theme.

nehemiah-9:16:25.summary: Proverb warns about a “stiff-necked man”; general wisdom only.

nehemiah-9:16:26.summary: Moses asks God to overlook “the hardness of this people”; general stubbornness theme.

nehemiah-9:16:27.summary: Hezekiah urges “do not harden your necks”; same idiom in a later appeal.
nehemiah-9:16:27.why: Later call to avoid the fathers’ sin.

nehemiah-9:16:28.summary: Stephen: “You stiff-necked people... as your fathers did”, charging the same ancestral stubbornness.
nehemiah-9:16:28.why: New Testament recital of the fathers’ rebellion.

nehemiah-9:17:2.summary: “Compassionate and merciful... patient and abundant in mercy”, the same divine attribute formula.
nehemiah-9:17:2.why: The classic confession of God’s character.

nehemiah-9:17:3.summary: “Compassionate and merciful, long-suffering, abundant in mercy”, matching Nehemiah’s formula.

nehemiah-9:17:11.summary: “Compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy”, God not dealing with us by our sins.

nehemiah-9:17:0.summary: God “abundant in mercy” and forbearing; partial echo of the formula.

nehemiah-9:17:1.summary: “Merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy”, the same attribute formula.
nehemiah-9:17:1.why: Prophetic use of the mercy formula.

nehemiah-9:17:4.summary: God desires mercy and passes over sins; mercy theme without the formula.

nehemiah-9:17:6.summary: Disciples do not “remember” the loaves; parallel failure to remember God’s wonders.
nehemiah-9:17:6.why: New Testament analog of forgetting miracles.

nehemiah-9:17:7.summary: Return to the Lord and “he will receive mercy”; general mercy and forgiveness.

nehemiah-9:17:9.summary: “He is compassionate” and would “not destroy” the rebellious wilderness generation.
nehemiah-9:17:9.why: Same pattern of mercy after rebellion.

nehemiah-9:17:10.summary: God’s words to Moses on mercy and compassion; general mercy theme.

nehemiah-9:17:12.summary: “They did not remember His hand” nor His signs in Egypt, matching forgetting God’s wonders.

nehemiah-9:17:13.summary: “Long-suffering, and abundant in mercy” in Moses’ plea after the wilderness rebellion.
nehemiah-9:17:13.why: The formula’s use in the original episode.

nehemiah-9:17:14.summary: Prayer that God “not abandon us”; echo of “didst not abandon them”.

nehemiah-9:17:15.summary: Despite provocations, God acted “according to His abundant mercy”, the same pattern.
nehemiah-9:17:15.why: Psalm parallel of mercy despite rebellion.

nehemiah-9:17:16.summary: Fathers “did not remember” God’s wonders in Egypt and provoked Him.

nehemiah-9:17:17.summary: They “forgot His benefits and the wonders He showed them”.
nehemiah-9:17:17.why: Psalm parallel to not remembering wonders.

nehemiah-9:17:18.summary: They “forgot His works”; general forgetfulness theme.

nehemiah-9:17:19.summary: Praise of grace and forgiveness in Christ; only a general mercy theme with no specific link.

nehemiah-9:17:20.summary: They despised the land and “did not hear the Lord’s voice”, the same wilderness refusal.
nehemiah-9:17:20.why: Psalm on the refusal to enter.

nehemiah-9:17:22.summary: “With Thee is atonement”; general forgiveness theme.

nehemiah-9:17:23.summary: Dathan and Abiram’s “We will not come up!”, an instance of refusal in the wilderness.

nehemiah-9:17:24.summary: “You did not obey” when called; general refusal to listen.
nehemiah-9:17:24.why: Wisdom’s parallel to refusing to hear.

nehemiah-9:17:25.summary: God asks how long they will refuse “despite all the signs I have done among them”, the Kadesh rebellion.
nehemiah-9:17:25.why: The original episode of forgotten wonders.

nehemiah-9:17:26.summary: Fathers refused to obey and “turned in their hearts toward Egypt”, like returning to slavery.
nehemiah-9:17:26.why: Stephen’s recital of the same rebellion.

nehemiah-9:17:27.summary: Warning not to “refuse the One who speaks”; general theme.

nehemiah-9:17:28.summary: Moses rebukes transgressing “the Lord’s word” in the Kadesh episode; loose link.

nehemiah-9:17:29.summary: Peter’s intent to remind readers; only incidental “remember” theme, no link to Israel’s rebellion.

nehemiah-9:18:0.summary: “They made a calf at Horeb” and forgot the God who saved them from Egypt.
nehemiah-9:18:0.why: Psalm recital of the golden calf.

nehemiah-9:18:2.summary: Moses confesses the people “made themselves gods of gold”, a great sin.

nehemiah-9:18:3.summary: Ezekiel recounts Israel’s rebellion in Egypt and wilderness; shown text (truncated) lacks the calf.

nehemiah-9:18:4.summary: Israel “made for themselves a molten image” at Sinai, the cast calf.

nehemiah-9:19:2.summary: Same prayer: “pillar of cloud by day... pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way”.

nehemiah-9:19:0.summary: “In Thy great compassion” God gave saviors; same refrain, different period.

nehemiah-9:19:1.summary: God relented “according to His abundant mercy”; general mercy theme.

nehemiah-9:19:3.summary: God’s unchanging nature; no shared element with the wilderness guidance.

nehemiah-9:19:4.summary: “A pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night” going before Israel.
nehemiah-9:19:4.why: Moses’ plea citing the same guidance.

nehemiah-9:19:5.summary: Daniel appeals to God’s “mercy, not our righteous deeds”; general mercy theme.

nehemiah-9:19:6.summary: “To the Lord belong righteousness and mercy”; general mercy theme.

nehemiah-9:19:7.summary: Cloud “by day” and fire “by night” over the tent throughout their journeys.
nehemiah-9:19:7.why: Narrative of the guiding cloud and fire.

nehemiah-9:19:8.summary: God saved provoking fathers for His name’s sake; mercy theme only.

nehemiah-9:19:11.summary: Fathers were “all under the cloud”, recalling the pillar of cloud.
nehemiah-9:19:11.why: Paul’s typological reading of the cloud.

nehemiah-9:19:12.summary: “In Thine abundant compassion” God did not “abandon” them, the same phrase.
nehemiah-9:19:12.why: Repeated refrain in the same prayer.

nehemiah-9:19:13.summary: Call for Israel to remember it is God’s servant; no link to cloud, fire or compassion.

nehemiah-9:19:14.summary: Cloud by day and “appearance of fire by night” guided Israel’s camping and travel.
nehemiah-9:19:14.why: Detailed account of the guiding pillar.

nehemiah-9:19:15.summary: A cloud “by day” and “light of fire burning by night” over Zion recalls the wilderness pillar.
nehemiah-9:19:15.why: Prophetic renewal of the Exodus pillar.

nehemiah-9:19:16.summary: God spared Israel for His name’s sake in the wilderness; mercy despite rebellion.
nehemiah-9:19:16.why: Explains why God did not abandon them.

nehemiah-9:19:17.summary: God held back for His name’s sake toward the wilderness generation.

nehemiah-9:19:18.summary: “The Lord will not reject His people”; echo of not abandoning them.

nehemiah-9:20:1.summary: God puts the Spirit upon the elders in the wilderness, an instance of giving His Spirit to Israel.
nehemiah-9:20:1.why: Concrete wilderness gift of the Spirit.

nehemiah-9:20:2.summary: God “placed the holy spirit among them” and a spirit guided them through the wilderness.
nehemiah-9:20:2.why: Prophetic recital of the Spirit in the Exodus.

nehemiah-9:20:3.summary: Jesus offers “living water”; water gift theme applied spiritually.
nehemiah-9:20:3.why: Christ as giver of true water.

nehemiah-9:20:4.summary: The Holy Spirit moved prophets; general theme of the Spirit instructing.

nehemiah-9:20:5.summary: God will “bring water out of a rock” for thirsting people in the wilderness.
nehemiah-9:20:5.why: Prophetic echo of the Exodus water.

nehemiah-9:20:6.summary: God answers thirst by opening rivers in the wilderness; general provision theme.

nehemiah-9:20:7.summary: Moses strikes the rock at Horeb and “water shall come forth” for the people to drink.

nehemiah-9:20:8.summary: “He split a rock, and waters flowed”, the water given for thirst.
nehemiah-9:20:8.why: Psalm recital of the same gift.

nehemiah-9:20:9.summary: Fruit of light in “goodness”; only an incidental word link to “good Spirit”.

nehemiah-9:20:10.summary: Manna named as “the bread the Lord has given you to eat”.

nehemiah-9:20:11.summary: Jesus links thirst-quenching water with the Spirit; thematic pairing of Spirit and water.
nehemiah-9:20:11.why: Christian fulfillment of Spirit and water.

nehemiah-9:20:12.summary: Water that ends thirst forever; general thirst and water theme.

nehemiah-9:20:13.summary: The manna ceased only after Israel ate the land’s grain, implying it was not withheld in the wilderness.
nehemiah-9:20:13.why: Marks the end of the manna provision.

nehemiah-9:20:14.summary: Same prayer: God testified “by Thy Spirit through Thy prophets”, another instance of His Spirit instructing Israel.
nehemiah-9:20:14.why: Links the Spirit’s teaching across Israel’s history.

nehemiah-9:20:15.summary: Promise they will “neither hunger nor thirst” and be led to springs; general provision theme.

nehemiah-9:20:16.summary: Israel “ate manna for forty years”, showing manna was not withheld.

nehemiah-9:20:17.summary: Fruit of the Spirit includes “goodness”; only incidental word overlap with “good Spirit”.

nehemiah-9:20:18.summary: God put “the Spirit” upon the seventy elders in the wilderness, who prophesied.
nehemiah-9:20:18.why: Concrete wilderness gift of the Spirit.

nehemiah-9:20:19.summary: Paul appeals through “the love of the Spirit” for prayer; no link to the wilderness gifts.

nehemiah-9:21:2.summary: “Forty years in the wilderness; your garments did not grow old” and sandals did not wear away.
nehemiah-9:21:2.why: Moses’ original statement of the same care.

nehemiah-9:21:3.summary: Those seeking the Lord “will not lack any good thing”; general echo of “lacked nothing”.

nehemiah-9:21:4.summary: The “forty years” in the wilderness as punishment, contrasting God’s nourishing care.
nehemiah-9:21:4.why: Explains why the forty years occurred.

nehemiah-9:21:5.summary: “For about forty years” God bore with them in the wilderness; general recap.
nehemiah-9:21:5.why: Paul’s summary of the wilderness period.

nehemiah-9:21:6.summary: Remember “the way wherein the Lord your God led you in the wilderness”; general wilderness theme.

nehemiah-9:21:7.summary: Israel “ate manna for forty years”, the nourishment Nehemiah recalls.

nehemiah-9:21:8.summary: Mentions Israel “in the wilderness for forty years” but about sacrifices, not provision.

nehemiah-9:22:1.summary: God routs Canaanite kings with hailstones; general conquest theme, not Sihon or Og.

nehemiah-9:22:2.summary: God killed “Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan” and gave their land as inheritance.
nehemiah-9:22:2.why: Psalm praise of the same victories.

nehemiah-9:22:3.summary: God threatens to “scatter them”; the Greek-based wording carries no link to apportioning conquered lands.
nehemiah-9:22:3.why: Label depends on Hebrew wording not present.

nehemiah-9:22:4.summary: God awakes like a mighty man; no shared element with the land grants of Sihon and Og.

nehemiah-9:22:5.summary: “He gave them countries of nations, and they inherited” the peoples’ toils.
nehemiah-9:22:5.why: Psalm parallel of God giving kingdoms.

nehemiah-9:22:6.summary: Joshua gave the land “as an inheritance” divided by tribes, God apportioning it.

nehemiah-9:22:7.summary: Account of Israel’s dealings with “Sihon king of Heshbon” (Seon of Esebon).
nehemiah-9:22:7.why: Narrative of the conquest of Sihon.

nehemiah-9:22:8.summary: God killed “Sihon king of the Amorites” and “Og king of Bashan” and gave their land as inheritance.
nehemiah-9:22:8.why: Liturgical praise of the same events.

nehemiah-9:22:9.summary: Narrative of the defeat of “Og king of Bashan” and seizure of his cities.
nehemiah-9:22:9.why: Account of the conquest of Og.

nehemiah-9:23:0.summary: God promises to “multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven” and to inherit.

nehemiah-9:23:2.summary: “To your seed I will give this land”, the land spoken of to the fathers.

nehemiah-9:23:3.summary: The Lord said He would “multiply Israel like the stars of heaven”.
nehemiah-9:23:3.why: Shows the star promise recalled later.

nehemiah-9:23:4.summary: Land promised to Isaac and his seed, confirming the oath to Abraham.
nehemiah-9:23:4.why: Shows the promise to the fathers.

nehemiah-9:23:5.summary: God brings the people across the Jordan into “the land that I am giving them”, as spoken.
nehemiah-9:23:5.why: Fulfillment of entry into the land.

nehemiah-9:23:6.summary: “All the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession” promised to Abraham’s seed.

nehemiah-9:23:7.summary: Covenant: “To your seed I will give this land”, spoken to the fathers.
nehemiah-9:23:7.why: Covenant origin of the land promise.

nehemiah-9:23:8.summary: Land promised to Abram’s seed, made numerous like sand.

nehemiah-9:24:0.summary: The Lord gave Israel the land sworn to their fathers; “they inherited it”.
nehemiah-9:24:0.why: Summary statement of the conquest’s fulfillment.

nehemiah-9:24:1.summary: “The land was held under their control” at Shiloh; general conquest result.

nehemiah-9:24:3.summary: God “has given the land’s inhabitants into hands”, similar wording but in David’s time.
nehemiah-9:24:3.why: Shows the same formula of subjugation.

nehemiah-9:24:4.summary: “Thy hand destroyed nations” and planted the fathers; they did not inherit by the sword.

nehemiah-9:24:5.summary: None of God’s good words failed; general fulfillment theme.
nehemiah-9:24:5.why: Affirms promise kept in the conquest.

nehemiah-9:24:6.summary: Escaping the devil’s snare “to do his will”; only incidental wording overlap.

nehemiah-9:24:7.summary: The children “shall inherit the land”; about entry, not the defeat of the Canaanites.

nehemiah-9:25:0.summary: Jacob “ate and was filled... grew fat” and forsook God, the same sequence.

nehemiah-9:25:1.summary: Same prayer: “Thine abundant goodness” in a broad and fertile land.

nehemiah-9:25:2.summary: Og’s “fortified cities, with high walls” were taken; partial echo of lofty cities.

nehemiah-9:25:4.summary: A land “flowing with milk and honey” prepared for Israel; general land-bounty theme.

nehemiah-9:25:5.summary: God fed them the produce of the fields, honey and oil, just before they grew fat.
nehemiah-9:25:5.why: Song of Moses on the land’s abundance.

nehemiah-9:25:6.summary: Plains “filled with richness” from God’s kindness; general bounty theme.

nehemiah-9:25:7.summary: Israel will marvel at the Lord’s “good things”; general goodness theme.

nehemiah-9:25:8.summary: People glad for “the good that the Lord had done”; general goodness theme.

nehemiah-9:25:9.summary: Israel to inherit nations with “cities great and walled up to heaven”; partial echo of lofty cities.

nehemiah-9:25:10.summary: Good land of vines, olives and fruit where “you shall eat and be filled”.

nehemiah-9:25:11.summary: Spies report fruitful land and fortified cities; general background.

nehemiah-9:25:12.summary: Despising “the wealth of His kindness”; general theme of abused goodness.

nehemiah-9:25:13.summary: “My people will be filled with My good things”; general echo.

nehemiah-9:25:14.summary: Houses “full of deceit” made them rich; loose contrast to houses full of good things.

nehemiah-9:25:15.summary: “They were filled to fullness, and their hearts were lifted up; ... they forgot Me.”
nehemiah-9:25:15.why: Same pattern of satiety leading to forgetting God.

nehemiah-9:25:16.summary: The people’s heart “has grown dull”; the Greek-based wording lacks the “fat” image the link assumes.
nehemiah-9:25:16.why: Link depends on Hebrew wording not present.

nehemiah-9:26:1.summary: Israel “forsook the Lord” and “provoked the Lord” after entering the land.

nehemiah-9:26:2.summary: Same prayer: “committed great provocations” at the calf.

nehemiah-9:26:3.summary: Stephen: the fathers “killed those who announced beforehand”, persecuting the prophets.
nehemiah-9:26:3.why: New Testament charge of killing prophets.

nehemiah-9:26:4.summary: Jezebel was “striking the Lord’s prophets”, an instance of killing God’s prophets.

nehemiah-9:26:5.summary: Israel “abandoned Thee” and “killed Thy prophets with the sword”.

nehemiah-9:26:6.summary: “Cast My words behind you”, matching casting God’s law behind them.
nehemiah-9:26:6.why: Same image of rejecting God’s word.

nehemiah-9:26:7.summary: Tenants beat and killed the owner’s slaves; parable echoing the killing of messengers.

nehemiah-9:26:9.summary: Jerusalem “kills the prophets and stones those sent to her”.
nehemiah-9:26:9.why: Jesus’ indictment of the same pattern.

nehemiah-9:26:10.summary: The children “did not walk in My commands”; general disobedience theme in the wilderness.

nehemiah-9:26:11.summary: Jezebel “was killing the Lord’s prophets”; Obadiah hid a hundred.

nehemiah-9:26:12.summary: Priests “set aside My law”; general corruption theme (truncated).

nehemiah-9:26:13.summary: They mocked “His prophets” and despised His words until wrath came.

nehemiah-9:26:14.summary: Watchman’s warning ignored; only a general idea of heedlessness, no shared element.

nehemiah-9:26:15.summary: “You have forsaken Me and served other gods”; general apostasy theme.

nehemiah-9:26:16.summary: Israel “forgot the Lord” and served the Baalim; general apostasy theme.

nehemiah-9:26:17.summary: Psalm recounts Israel’s idolatry in the land after the conquest, provoking wrath.
nehemiah-9:26:17.why: Parallel recital of the same apostasy.

nehemiah-9:26:18.summary: “They abandoned the Lord and did not serve Him”; general apostasy theme.

nehemiah-9:26:19.summary: King Jehoiakim killed the prophet Uriah with the sword.
nehemiah-9:26:19.why: Concrete case of a prophet killed.

nehemiah-9:26:20.summary: They “turned back and broke faith” and “changed into a crooked bow”, echoing they “changed and withdrew”.

nehemiah-9:26:21.summary: Same prayer: God testified through His prophets but they did not give ear.
nehemiah-9:26:21.why: Continues the theme of rejected prophets.

nehemiah-9:26:22.summary: Allegory of Samaria and Jerusalem’s prostitution; general apostasy theme (truncated).

nehemiah-9:26:23.summary: Manasseh’s abominations caused Judah to sin; general apostasy example.

nehemiah-9:26:24.summary: Jerusalem’s idolatrous prostitution with God’s gifts; general apostasy theme (truncated).

nehemiah-9:27:0.summary: God “handed them over into nations’ hands”, heard their petition and rescued them by abundant mercy.
nehemiah-9:27:0.why: Psalm recital of the same cycle.

nehemiah-9:27:1.summary: Daniel confesses disobedience bringing calamities; similar penitential theme, not the deliverance cycle.

nehemiah-9:27:2.summary: The Lord gave Israel “deliverance” from Syria’s hand; an instance of rescue.

nehemiah-9:27:3.summary: God “saved them through Jeroboam”; example of a saviour figure.

nehemiah-9:27:4.summary: Israel cries out in distress and God grows weary over “Israel’s distress”.

nehemiah-9:27:5.summary: Israel “cried out to the Lord” under Midian; God rescued from “all who oppressed you”.
nehemiah-9:27:5.why: Judges instance of the same pattern.

nehemiah-9:27:7.summary: Seeking the Lord “in your distress”, for He is “a merciful God” who will not forsake.

nehemiah-9:27:8.summary: Israel cried out and “the Lord raised up a saviour”, Othniel, who saved them.
nehemiah-9:27:8.why: First judges example of God’s saviours.

nehemiah-9:27:9.summary: God “handed everything into their hands” to the Chaldeans; giving into enemies’ hands only.

nehemiah-9:27:10.summary: Greek-based text has “men who have been saved”, not saviours, so the label’s link is lost.

nehemiah-9:27:12.summary: They cried to the Lord and He sent Jerubbaal, Barak, Jephthah and Samuel to rescue them.

nehemiah-9:27:13.summary: God foretells forsaking Israel to afflictions for apostasy; judgment side only.

nehemiah-9:28:0.summary: The land was quiet forty years, then Israel “did evil” and was given to Midian.

nehemiah-9:28:1.summary: Israel defeated by enemies cries out and God will “hear from heaven” and be merciful.

nehemiah-9:28:2.summary: “The land was quiet for eighty years” after Ehud; the rest phase only.
nehemiah-9:28:2.why: Shows a rest period in Judges.

nehemiah-9:28:4.summary: “The sons of Israel again did evil before the Lord”, the relapse after rest.

nehemiah-9:28:5.summary: “Hear from heaven” in Solomon’s prayer; general phrase overlap.

nehemiah-9:28:6.summary: “Many times He rescued them” according to “His abundant mercy”.
nehemiah-9:28:6.why: Psalm summary of the repeated rescues.

nehemiah-9:28:7.summary: Appeal to God from heaven for “abundance of Thy mercy and compassion”.

nehemiah-9:29:1.summary: Same prayer: “stiffened their necks and did not listen to Thy commandments”.

nehemiah-9:29:2.summary: Prophets “testified among them to turn them back to Thee”, the same phrase.

nehemiah-9:29:3.summary: Links on “acted arrogantly”, a phrase absent from the Saints wording of this verse.
nehemiah-9:29:3.why: Link depends on wording not present.

nehemiah-9:29:4.summary: Leaders reject Jeremiah’s word; refusal to heed, without the arrogance wording the label assumes.

nehemiah-9:29:5.summary: God “mowed down” through prophets’ words; no real link to Israel’s refusal to listen.

nehemiah-9:29:6.summary: Call to humility against pride; the source lacks the pride wording, leaving only general theme.

nehemiah-9:29:7.summary: They “turned a senseless back” so as not to listen to the law sent through the prophets.

nehemiah-9:29:8.summary: Prophets sent “to turn them back”; “They testified to them, but they did not listen.”

nehemiah-9:29:9.summary: “Hear and give ear” and warning of consequences; general theme.

nehemiah-9:29:10.summary: “The one who does these things will live by them”, the same law formula.
nehemiah-9:29:10.why: Paul’s use of the same principle.

nehemiah-9:29:11.summary: Not holding fast “to My ordinances” set before their fathers; general theme.

nehemiah-9:29:12.summary: “They did not hear Me... and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers.”

nehemiah-9:29:13.summary: The song will witness against them; testimony theme, loosely related.

nehemiah-9:29:14.summary: “They hardened their necks so as not to listen to My words.”

nehemiah-9:29:15.summary: People tell Jeremiah “we will not listen to you”; general refusal theme.

nehemiah-9:29:16.summary: “Do this and you will live” echoes commandments a person “does” and “will live by them”.
nehemiah-9:29:16.why: Jesus affirms the same law principle.

nehemiah-9:29:17.summary: Pharaoh refusing to reverence God; the Greek-based wording of the source lacks the pride link and the subject differs.

nehemiah-9:29:18.summary: God “sent through prophets, rising early”, sparing His people; general theme of prophetic warning.

nehemiah-9:29:19.summary: God calls heaven and earth “to witness against you”; testimony theme only.

nehemiah-9:29:20.summary: “The person who does these things will live by them”, the same law formula.

nehemiah-9:29:21.summary: God sent prophets saying “Turn, each from his evil way”, and “you did not listen”.

nehemiah-9:29:22.summary: God warned through prophets, “Turn... keep My commandments, My ordinances, and all the law”.

nehemiah-9:29:24.summary: Ordinances “which a person will carry out and by which he will live”.

nehemiah-9:29:25.summary: “They hardened their neck... so as not to hear Me”, the same idiom.

nehemiah-9:30:0.summary: God’s “forbearance and patience”; general echo of prolonged dealings.
nehemiah-9:30:0.why: New Testament view of divine patience.

nehemiah-9:30:1.summary: They “provoked His holy spirit” and He fought them; loose Spirit and judgment theme.
nehemiah-9:30:1.why: Rejection of the Spirit brings judgment.

nehemiah-9:30:2.summary: God warned through “all His prophets”, but “they did not listen”, leading to exile.
nehemiah-9:30:2.why: Narrative of the same rejection and judgment.

nehemiah-9:30:3.summary: “You always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did”, tying the Spirit to rejected prophets.

nehemiah-9:30:5.summary: God “gave Jacob over to plunder” because they refused to “listen to His law”.

nehemiah-9:30:6.summary: The Spirit of Christ in the prophets “testified beforehand”; Spirit-in-prophets theme only.

nehemiah-9:30:7.summary: The Lord fulfilled His words and exalted the oppressor; general judgment theme.

nehemiah-9:30:8.summary: “He spoke and they did not listen”; general refusal theme.

nehemiah-9:30:9.summary: Prophets spoke “borne along by the Holy Spirit”; general Spirit-and-prophets theme.

nehemiah-9:30:10.summary: Same prayer: prophets “testified among them”, but were killed.

nehemiah-9:30:11.summary: God kept “sending My servants the prophets... and you did not listen”.

nehemiah-9:30:12.summary: God abandons His vineyard to be plundered; general judgment image.

nehemiah-9:30:13.summary: Same prayer: God testified to them, “but they did not listen”.

nehemiah-9:30:14.summary: Since the Exodus God “sent out to you all My servants the prophets”, over many years.
nehemiah-9:30:14.why: Shows the long span of prophetic witness.

nehemiah-9:30:15.summary: “The Holy Spirit spoke well through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers”, the Spirit through prophets.
nehemiah-9:30:15.why: New Testament statement of the same idea.

nehemiah-9:30:16.summary: God “put up with their conduct” forty years; general forbearance theme.

nehemiah-9:30:17.summary: Same prayer mentions “Thy good Spirit” given for understanding; partial echo.
nehemiah-9:30:17.why: Links Spirit in wilderness and prophets.

nehemiah-9:30:18.summary: God is “long-suffering”; general echo of prolonged dealings.

nehemiah-9:30:19.summary: Calamities came because they “did not obey His voice”; general judgment theme.

nehemiah-9:30:20.summary: “The Lord could no longer bear” their wickedness, the end of His prolonged patience.

nehemiah-9:30:21.summary: The Lord “is patient toward you”; general forbearance theme.
nehemiah-9:30:21.why: New Testament view of God’s patience.

nehemiah-9:31:4.summary: “Compassionate and merciful” Lord who will not be angry to the end.

nehemiah-9:31:7.summary: “Compassionate and merciful is the Lord”, matching “merciful and compassionate”.

nehemiah-9:31:1.summary: Same prayer: “a merciful and compassionate God... didst not abandon them”.

nehemiah-9:31:2.summary: God proclaims Himself “compassionate and merciful... abundant in mercy”, the source formula.

nehemiah-9:31:3.summary: “I will certainly not make a complete end”, despite judgment.

nehemiah-9:31:5.summary: “I will certainly not bring you to a complete end.”

nehemiah-9:31:6.summary: “Do not make a complete end” of Jerusalem.

nehemiah-9:31:8.summary: Survivors left in Jerusalem after judgment; general remnant theme.

nehemiah-9:31:9.summary: “The Lord our God is merciful and compassionate; He will not turn His face from us.”

nehemiah-9:31:10.summary: The Lord had mercy and “was unwilling to destroy them”.
nehemiah-9:31:10.why: Historical instance of the same mercy.

nehemiah-9:31:11.summary: “To the Lord belong righteousness and mercy”; general mercy theme.

nehemiah-9:32:0.summary: God “who keeps covenant and mercy”, the same title.

nehemiah-9:32:1.summary: Nehemiah’s earlier prayer: “the Mighty One, the Great and Fearsome, who dost keep the covenant and mercy”.

nehemiah-9:32:3.summary: God grants mercy sworn to the fathers; general covenant mercy theme.

nehemiah-9:32:4.summary: Shame belongs “to our kings, rulers, and fathers”, a similar list in confession.

nehemiah-9:32:6.summary: God “fearsome in His counsels”; shares only the attribute.

nehemiah-9:32:7.summary: “How fearsome are Thy works”; shares only the attribute.

nehemiah-9:32:8.summary: God “keeping covenant and mercy” with His servants, the same title.

nehemiah-9:32:9.summary: Assyrian king Thaglathphellasar deported Naphtali, a hardship from “the kings of Assour”.

nehemiah-9:32:10.summary: The Assyrians as “the rod of My anger” against Israel; prophetic background.

nehemiah-9:32:11.summary: Zedekiah’s sons killed and he blinded; an example of hardship on kings, Babylonian not Assyrian.

nehemiah-9:32:12.summary: Gedaliah murdered and the people flee to Egypt; general post-exile hardship.

nehemiah-9:32:13.summary: Josiah killed by Nechao; hardship on a king, Egyptian not Assyrian.

nehemiah-9:32:14.summary: Nechao deposes Joachas and imposes tribute; general hardship example.

nehemiah-9:32:15.summary: Prophecy that God will bring “the king of the Assyrians” upon Judah.

nehemiah-9:32:16.summary: Bones of “kings... rulers... priests... prophets” and inhabitants, a matching list of those under judgment.

nehemiah-9:32:17.summary: God will discipline “seven times according to your sins”; covenant curse background.

nehemiah-9:32:18.summary: Babylon besieges and breaches Jerusalem (truncated); general hardship.

nehemiah-9:32:19.summary: God will add “seven blows” for disobedience; covenant curse background.

nehemiah-9:32:20.summary: Discipline “seven times more” for sins; covenant curse background.

nehemiah-9:32:21.summary: God described as “a great and mighty God”; partial echo of the titles.

nehemiah-9:32:22.summary: Phul king of the Assyrians invaded and exacted tribute, an early Assyrian hardship.

nehemiah-9:32:23.summary: Priests and officials executed by Babylon’s king; hardship on priests.

nehemiah-9:32:24.summary: The Lord is “fearsome, a great King”; partial echo of the titles.

nehemiah-9:32:25.summary: The Lord brings “the king of the Assyrians” over Judah; prophetic background.

nehemiah-9:32:26.summary: God will strike “seven times” for sins; covenant curse background.

nehemiah-9:32:27.summary: Fall of Jerusalem under Zedekiah (truncated); general hardship on king and people.

nehemiah-9:32:28.summary: Rulers, priests and Zedekiah handed to enemies; similar classes under judgment.

nehemiah-9:32:29.summary: Salamanasar king of the Assyrians subjugated Hoshea, a hardship from Assyrian kings.

nehemiah-9:32:30.summary: Jehoiakim’s shameful burial; hardship of a king only.

nehemiah-9:32:31.summary: Ezra confesses what came “through our evil deeds”; similar penitential theme.

nehemiah-9:32:32.summary: Sennacherib “king of the Assyrians” takes Judea’s fortified cities.

nehemiah-9:32:33.summary: Last kings of Judah deposed and exiled (truncated); general hardship.

nehemiah-9:33:0.summary: “We sinned with our fathers”; similar confession of sin.

nehemiah-9:33:1.summary: Abraham affirms the Judge of all the earth will do justice; general theme.

nehemiah-9:33:2.summary: “Righteousness belongs to Thee, Lord, but shame of face to us”, because we sinned.

nehemiah-9:33:3.summary: God observes everyone; no shared element with confessing God’s righteousness.

nehemiah-9:33:4.summary: “Thou art righteous, Lord, and Thy judgment is upright.”

nehemiah-9:33:5.summary: “Thou art righteous, Lord”, but in a complaint about the wicked prospering.

nehemiah-9:33:6.summary: They “shall confess their sins and their fathers’ sins”, as Nehemiah’s people do.

nehemiah-9:33:7.summary: “The Lord is righteous, for I embittered His mouth”, owning guilt amid calamity.
nehemiah-9:33:7.why: Same justification of God in suffering.

nehemiah-9:33:8.summary: A man blames himself, not punished as sins deserved; general confession theme.

nehemiah-9:33:9.summary: “The Lord is righteous in all His ways”, echoing righteous “in all”.

nehemiah-9:34:2.summary: The song bears “witness” against Israel; general testimony theme.

nehemiah-9:34:3.summary: Same prayer: God did “testify to them” through prophets, but they did not give ear.

nehemiah-9:35:0.summary: “You did not serve the Lord... for the abundance of all things.”
nehemiah-9:35:0.why: The curse matching the failure confessed.

nehemiah-9:35:1.summary: They served foreign gods in their land; general failure to serve God.

nehemiah-9:35:2.summary: God fed them richly and Jacob grew fat and “forsook God”, rebellion amid abundance.
nehemiah-9:35:2.why: Song of Moses on the same pattern.

nehemiah-9:35:3.summary: “A good and spacious land” of plenty, matching the broad and fertile land.

nehemiah-9:35:4.summary: Same prayer: they lived in luxury “in Thy great goodness”.

nehemiah-9:35:5.summary: God knows their wickedness before bringing them into “the good land”; general theme.

nehemiah-9:35:6.summary: God’s righteousness versus human unrighteousness; no specific link to failing to serve amid abundance.

nehemiah-9:36:1.summary: “You shall serve your enemies” in want, the covenant curse behind “we are slaves today”.

nehemiah-9:36:2.summary: They “will become servants” of the kingdoms of the earth.
nehemiah-9:36:2.why: Servitude to foreign kings as discipline.

nehemiah-9:37:1.summary: Serving enemies sent by the Lord, matching kings set over them for their sins.

nehemiah-9:37:2.summary: Persian decree on taxes and authority over temple servants; loose link to foreign authority.

nehemiah-9:37:3.summary: Claim to “have never been slaves”, contrasting Nehemiah’s “we are slaves”.
nehemiah-9:37:3.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

nehemiah-9:37:4.summary: Taxes owed to kings from Jerusalem; loose link to kings taking produce.

nehemiah-9:37:5.summary: Jews sold to nations and bought back; general servitude theme.

nehemiah-9:37:6.summary: Planting vineyards without enjoying them; curse of losing the land’s fruit.

nehemiah-9:37:7.summary: Royal taxes funding the temple; no real link to kings oppressing bodies and livestock.

nehemiah-9:37:8.summary: Falling before enemies who pursue; general curse of subjugation.

nehemiah-9:37:9.summary: A foreign nation consumes “the offspring of your cattle and the produce of your land”.
nehemiah-9:37:9.why: Curse matching loss of livestock and produce.

nehemiah-10:1:0.summary: The next verse lists “those sealing,” beginning with Neemias, who seal the pledge.
nehemiah-10:1:0.why: Names the signers of the pledge.

nehemiah-10:1:1.summary: Ezra’s people also “make a covenant with our God” to act according to the law.
nehemiah-10:1:1.why: Earlier covenant renewal in the return.

nehemiah-10:1:2.summary: The people enter “a curse and an oath to walk in the law of God,” the content of the sealed pledge.

nehemiah-10:1:3.summary: Josiah “established a covenant before the Lord” to keep His commandments, a parallel renewal.

nehemiah-10:1:4.summary: Jehoiada made a covenant that the people “should be the Lord’s people,” a parallel renewal.

nehemiah-10:1:5.summary: Hezekiah resolves “to establish a covenant of the Lord” to turn away wrath, paralleling the pledge.

nehemiah-10:1:6.summary: Josiah “made a covenant before the Lord” and “All the people stood in the covenant.”

nehemiah-10:1:7.summary: Asa’s people “passed into a covenant to seek the Lord,” a parallel communal pledge.

nehemiah-10:2:0.summary: The preceding verse introduces the written pledge that these men are “sealing.”
nehemiah-10:2:0.why: Gives the context of the signatures.

nehemiah-10:2:1.summary: “Neemias” appears again with Ezra leading the reading of the law.

nehemiah-10:2:3.summary: “Athersatha” is a governor’s title, not clearly tied to Nehemiah in the shown text.

nehemiah-10:2:4.summary: Family heads gave to “Neemia” for the work, the same leader who signs first.

nehemiah-10:3:0.summary: “Saraia” also appears in the priestly genealogy, but identity with the signer is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:3:2.summary: “Azarias” and “Jermia” both appear among priests at the wall’s dedication, but identity is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:3:3.summary: An “Azaria” repaired the wall, but identity with the signer is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:4:1.summary: A “Melchias” stood with Ezra, but identity with the signer is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:4:2.summary: “Phassour” and “Melchia” appear together in a priestly genealogy, suggesting the same priestly families.

nehemiah-10:4:3.summary: A “Melchias” repaired the wall, but identity with the signer is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:5:2.summary: “Atous son of Asbania” resembles the signers “Atous, Sebani,” but identity is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:6:0.summary: The shown text, “Sechenia,” matches none of Iram, Meramoth or Abdia.
nehemiah-10:6:0.why: No shared name in the shown wording.

nehemiah-10:6:1.summary: “Eram” resembles “Iram,” but this is a patronym of a wall builder.

nehemiah-10:6:2.summary: “From Ramoth, a son of Ouria” may garble Meramoth son of Ouria, but the name is not shown.

nehemiah-10:6:3.summary: “Meramoth son of Ouria” repaired the wall, likely the priest Meramoth who signs.

nehemiah-10:7:1.summary: “Barouch son of Zabou” repaired the wall, possibly the signer Barouch.

nehemiah-10:8:0.summary: “Mosollam” stood with Ezra, but identity with the signer Mesoulam is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:8:2.summary: The shown priests include “Beniamin,” not Miamin, Abia or Mesoulam.
nehemiah-10:8:2.why: No shared name in the shown wording.

nehemiah-10:8:4.summary: “Mesoulam” appears in a priestly genealogy, but identity with the signer is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:8:5.summary: The shown portion of the dedication account names none of Mesoulam, Abia or Miamin; truncated range.
nehemiah-10:8:5.why: No shared name in the shown text.

nehemiah-10:8:6.summary: “Mesoulam son of Basodia” repaired a gate, possibly but not clearly the signer.

nehemiah-10:8:7.summary: “Mesoulam” heads a priestly house, possibly connected to the signer.

nehemiah-10:9:0.summary: “Masaia” and “Samaia” are priests in Ezra’s list, similar to the signers, but identity is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:9:3.summary: A “Samaia” repaired the wall, but identity with the priest is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:9:4.summary: “Maasias” and “Semeias” appear at the dedication, similar to Maazia and Samaia, but uncertain.

nehemiah-10:10:1.summary: Levites “Beni son of Enadad” and “son of Iesous” repaired the wall, matching the Enadad family and Jesus.
nehemiah-10:10:1.why: Shows the same Levite families at work.

nehemiah-10:10:2.summary: “Jesus and the sons of Kadmiel” lead the Levites in prayer, the same Levites who sign.

nehemiah-10:10:3.summary: “Jesou and the sons of Kadmiel” are rulers of the Levites, matching the signers.
nehemiah-10:10:3.why: Shows their role among the Levites.

nehemiah-10:10:4.summary: The Levites “Jesus, Banaias” helped the people understand the law, matching the signers Jesus and Banaiou.

nehemiah-10:10:6.summary: The returnee list names Levites “the sons of Jesus, belonging to Kadmiel,” the same families.
nehemiah-10:10:6.why: Traces these Levite families to the return.

nehemiah-10:11:0.summary: The shown names, Jesus, Banaias and Sarabia, match none of Sabania, Odouia, Kalita, Pheleia or Anan.
nehemiah-10:11:0.why: No shared name in the shown wording.

nehemiah-10:11:1.summary: The Levite “Kolitas” corresponds to the signer “Kalita,” named among the Levites.

nehemiah-10:11:2.summary: The same Levite group leads prayer, but none of the specific names in the source appear.

nehemiah-10:12:0.summary: “Samaia son of Asoub” matches none of Micha, Roob or Esebias.
nehemiah-10:12:0.why: No shared name in the shown wording.

nehemiah-10:12:1.summary: The Levite “Asebia” resembles “Esebias,” but identity is uncertain.

nehemiah-10:12:2.summary: “Asabia” resembles “Esebias,” but here appears among priests’ leaders.

nehemiah-10:12:3.summary: “Asabia” is named among rulers of the Levites, likely the signer Esebias.

nehemiah-10:12:4.summary: The Levite genealogy names “Asabia, son of Micha,” matching the signers Micha and Esebias.

nehemiah-10:13:0.summary: The Levite “Sarabia” is named among those leading prayer, matching the signer.

nehemiah-10:13:1.summary: The Levite “Sarabia” helped explain the law, matching the signer.

nehemiah-10:15:2.summary: The clan “Banoui” may be among the rulers, but the source’s list is cut off at “sons of.”

nehemiah-10:15:3.summary: The returnee list names “Phoros,” “Phaathmoab,” “Ailam” and “Zathoua,” the same clans as the signers; truncated range.
nehemiah-10:15:3.why: Traces the signers’ clans to the return.

nehemiah-10:15:4.summary: “Asoub son of Phaathmoab” repaired the wall, from the same clan Phaathmoab.
nehemiah-10:15:4.why: Shows the clan’s part in rebuilding.

nehemiah-10:16:0.summary: The clan “Babi” likely corresponds to Bebai, but the shown context is the foreign-wives list.

nehemiah-10:16:2.summary: “Babi” and “Asgad” appear together as clans with Ezra, matching the signers Bebai and Asgad.

nehemiah-10:17:2.summary: “The sons of Bago” returned with Ezra, the clan represented by the signer “Bagoi.”

nehemiah-10:19:0.summary: The returnee list includes “Basou” and “Asem,” matching the signers “Besi” and “Esam”; truncated range.
nehemiah-10:19:0.why: Traces these clans to the return.

nehemiah-10:26:0.summary: “Raoum son of Bani,” a Levite, repaired the wall, matching the signer “Raoum”; truncated range.

nehemiah-10:29:8.summary: Both list the same classes of the restored community—priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and Nathinim—but Ezra 2:70 describes resettlement, not the covenant pledge.
nehemiah-10:29:8.why: Shows the same community groups across Ezra–Nehemiah.

nehemiah-10:29:11.summary: Nehemiah 7:72–73 uses “the remainder of the people” and the same roster of priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers and Nathinim found in the covenant signers.
nehemiah-10:29:11.why: Links the covenant community to the returned exiles' roll.

nehemiah-10:29:0.summary: Nehemiah 9:2 belongs to the same assembly, where Israel separated from foreigners and confessed, leading to the pledge of those turning from the peoples of the land.
nehemiah-10:29:0.why: Sets the covenant pledge in its confession context.

nehemiah-10:29:1.summary: Paul's call to “be separated” from unbelievers echoes the idea of turning from the peoples of the land to God's law, but only thematically.
nehemiah-10:29:1.why: New Testament application of covenant separation.

nehemiah-10:29:2.summary: Jeremiah 4:2 concerns swearing “The Lord lives” in truth; Nehemiah 10:29 describes who joined the covenant, with no oath wording in this verse.

nehemiah-10:29:3.summary: Paul being “set apart for the gospel” shares only a general idea of separation, not present in the wording of Nehemiah 10:29.

nehemiah-10:29:4.summary: Ecclesiastes' warning against hasty words before God has no real connection to the list of those joining the covenant.

nehemiah-10:29:5.summary: “Make music with understanding” shares only the word understanding with “everyone knowing and understanding”; the contexts differ.

nehemiah-10:29:6.summary: Nehemiah 13:3 has people separating the mixed population on hearing the law, loosely paralleling turning from the peoples of the land to God's law.
nehemiah-10:29:6.why: Shows later enforcement of the same commitment.

nehemiah-10:29:7.summary: Both describe men, women and all who could understand gathered to the law of God, using closely matching language of understanding.
nehemiah-10:29:7.why: Connects the pledge to the public law reading.

nehemiah-10:29:9.summary: The shown portion of Ezra 2 lists priests, Levites, singers and gatekeepers, the same classes named, but as a census rather than a covenant (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:29:10.summary: Ezra 9:1–2 reports priests and Levites failing to separate from “the peoples of the lands,” the very issue the covenant community here addresses.
nehemiah-10:29:10.why: Shows the problem the covenant answers.

nehemiah-10:29:12.summary: God “separated you from all the nations” in Leviticus 20:24 underlies Israel's distinctness, but the link to this list is general.

nehemiah-10:29:13.summary: Ezra 10:11 commands, “Separate yourselves from the peoples of the land,” matching the covenant community's turning from those peoples to God's law.
nehemiah-10:29:13.why: Earlier reform with the same aim.

nehemiah-10:30:0.summary: Ezekiel 36:27 promises Israel will “walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments and do them,” echoing the pledge to walk in and keep God's judgments.
nehemiah-10:30:0.why: Prophetic promise matching the covenant vow.

nehemiah-10:30:1.summary: The psalmist has “sworn” to keep God's judgments, mirroring the oath to keep the Lord's commandments and judgments.
nehemiah-10:30:1.why: Personal parallel to the communal oath.

nehemiah-10:30:2.summary: Doing what Jesus commands loosely parallels pledging to keep all the Lord's commandments, but only as general obedience.

nehemiah-10:30:3.summary: Titus on grace training believers in godly living has no specific link to the oath to keep Moses' law.

nehemiah-10:30:4.summary: Josiah's covenant “to walk before the Lord and keep His commandments” is a closely parallel covenant-renewal pledge.
nehemiah-10:30:4.why: Earlier covenant renewal with the same vow.

nehemiah-10:30:5.summary: Josiah's covenant to keep the Lord's commandments, with all the people standing in it, parallels the community's oath to keep the law.

nehemiah-10:30:6.summary: Nehemiah 5:12–13 records an oath sealed with a curse on whoever fails to keep it, like the “curse and an oath” here.

nehemiah-10:30:7.summary: The Greek here says the people “prevailed over their brothers,” so Romans' “cling to what is good” carries no real link.
nehemiah-10:30:7.why: Label relies on Hebrew wording absent here.

nehemiah-10:30:8.summary: Malachi's call to remember “the law of Moses My servant… ordinances and judgments” echoes the law “given through Moses the slave of God.”
nehemiah-10:30:8.why: Prophetic summons to the same law.

nehemiah-10:30:9.summary: John 1:17 says “the Law was given through Moses,” closely echoing “the law of God given through Moses.”
nehemiah-10:30:9.why: Sets Moses' law beside grace in Christ.

nehemiah-10:30:10.summary: People joining Paul in Athens has no link; the Greek source speaks of prevailing over brothers, not joining.

nehemiah-10:30:11.summary: “Lord our Lord” in Psalm 8 shares only the phrase “our Lord,” with no thematic tie to the covenant oath.

nehemiah-10:30:12.summary: Jesus says Moses gave the Law yet none keeps it, contrasting with the pledge to keep Moses' law.
nehemiah-10:30:12.why: Highlights failure to keep the vowed law.

nehemiah-10:30:13.summary: Solomon's prayer mentions “walking in My law,” a stock phrase shared with the pledge, in a different context.

nehemiah-10:30:14.summary: Jeremiah warns those not “walking in My ordinances,” sharing covenant vocabulary but not context.
nehemiah-10:30:14.why: Shows consequences of neglecting the law.

nehemiah-10:30:15.summary: Moses tells Israel to learn “the ordinances and the judgments” and “do them,” the very law the people swear to keep.
nehemiah-10:30:15.why: Torah source of the vowed obligations.

nehemiah-10:30:16.summary: Psalm 104:45 states the purpose of keeping God's ordinances and law, a general echo of the pledge.

nehemiah-10:30:17.summary: Deuteronomy 27's ceremony of curses on law-breakers, affirmed by all the people, underlies entering “into a curse and an oath” to keep the law (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:30:18.summary: Nehemiah 13:25 has Nehemiah curse the people and make them swear by God, recalling this curse-and-oath covenant.
nehemiah-10:30:18.why: Later enforcement of the same oath.

nehemiah-10:30:19.summary: Under Asa the people swore by the Lord with a death penalty for those not seeking Him, a comparable sworn covenant.

nehemiah-10:30:20.summary: Jehu “did not take care to walk in the law of the Lord,” the opposite of the people's pledge.
nehemiah-10:30:20.why: Negative example of the same commitment.

nehemiah-10:30:21.summary: Isaiah 14:1 on foreigners joining Jacob's house has no specific link to the oath to keep God's law.

nehemiah-10:30:22.summary: The conspirators “bound themselves under a curse,” a similar oath-curse formula used for an evil purpose.

nehemiah-10:30:23.summary: Psalm 8's praise of the Lord's name shares only “our Lord” with the covenant pledge.

nehemiah-10:30:25.summary: Deuteronomy 33:4 speaks of “the law which Moses commanded us,” echoing the law given through Moses.

nehemiah-10:30:26.summary: The men who “bound themselves under a curse” use the same oath-curse form, in an unrelated plot.

nehemiah-10:30:27.summary: Barnabas urging believers to remain with the Lord has no link in the Greek source, which speaks of prevailing over brothers.

nehemiah-10:30:28.summary: Moses urges Israel to do as commanded without turning aside, a general parallel to the vow to keep all commandments.

nehemiah-10:31:1.summary: Exodus 34:16 forbids taking their daughters for your sons and giving your daughters to their sons, the law behind this pledge.

nehemiah-10:31:2.summary: Ezra 9:1–3 reports Israel taking daughters of the peoples of the lands, the exact problem this vow addresses.

nehemiah-10:31:3.summary: Esdras orders the people to separate from “the peoples of the land” and foreign wives, the same issue as the vow.

nehemiah-10:31:4.summary: Ezra 9:12 says, “do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take… their daughters for your sons,” nearly identical to the pledge.
nehemiah-10:31:4.why: Near-verbatim prior statement of the rule.

nehemiah-10:32:1.summary: Leviticus 23:3 commands Sabbath rest from work, the general law behind refusing Sabbath trade.

nehemiah-10:32:2.summary: Exodus 23:10–11 commands granting the land release in the seventh year, the basis for “we will release the seventh year.”
nehemiah-10:32:2.why: Torah source of the seventh-year pledge.

nehemiah-10:32:3.summary: The Sabbath commandment forbids work on the seventh day, the general basis for refusing to buy on the Sabbath.

nehemiah-10:32:4.summary: Jeremiah forbids carrying burdens through Jerusalem's gates on the Sabbath, the same concern with Sabbath commerce.

nehemiah-10:32:5.summary: Isaiah's call to “release the crushed” and tear up unjust contracts loosely parallels releasing every debt claim.

nehemiah-10:32:6.summary: The Day of Atonement forbids work, loosely relating to the pledge not to trade on a holy day.

nehemiah-10:32:8.summary: Deuteronomy's Sabbath command to do no work underlies the pledge, but does not address buying and selling.

nehemiah-10:32:9.summary: Leviticus 25 commands a Sabbath year in which the land rests, the law behind releasing the seventh year (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:32:10.summary: Exodus 12:16 forbids work on a “holy appointed day,” loosely linking to not trading on a holy day.

nehemiah-10:32:11.summary: Festival days with no laborious work relate generally to keeping holy days free of commerce.

nehemiah-10:32:12.summary: The land keeping its neglected Sabbaths during exile relates to the seventh-year pledge only by implication.
