nehemiah-10:32:13.summary: Deuteronomy 15:9 names “the seventh year, the year of release” for debts, matching the release of every hand's demand.

nehemiah-10:32:14.summary: Nehemiah 5 deals with pledged fields and debt slavery among Jews, the situation the debt-release pledge addresses (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:32:15.summary: Isaiah's call not to do one's own wishes on “the holy day” loosely parallels refusing trade on the Sabbath or holy day.

nehemiah-10:32:16.summary: A holy convocation day with no laborious work relates only generally to the pledge.

nehemiah-10:32:17.summary: “Forgive us our debts” echoes debt release only as a broad spiritual theme.

nehemiah-10:32:18.summary: The master who “released him and forgave him the loan” relates loosely to releasing every hand's demand (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:32:19.summary: Colossians mentions Sabbaths and festivals as matters not to judge by, a loose contrast with binding Sabbath vows.

nehemiah-10:32:20.summary: James on mercy triumphing over judgment has no specific link to Sabbath trade or debt release.

nehemiah-10:33:1.summary: Matthew 17 concerns collectors of “the didrachmas,” the annual temple tax echoed in giving part of a didrachm for God's house.

nehemiah-10:33:2.summary: Paul on giving according to means has no specific link to the fixed temple levy.

nehemiah-10:33:4.summary: Jacob's vow of a tenth for the “house of God” loosely parallels pledging support for God's house.

nehemiah-10:35:3.summary: A proverb that a lot settles disputes relates generally to casting lots to assign duties.

nehemiah-10:35:4.summary: The first lot falling to Jarib shows lots assigning priestly courses, a loose parallel to lots for the wood duty.

nehemiah-10:35:9.summary: Hebrews mentions sacrifices “year by year” and whole burnt offerings, a loose link to fueling the altar yearly.

nehemiah-10:36:0.summary: Deuteronomy 26:2 commands taking “the firstfruits of the produce of your land” to God's chosen place, as pledged here.

nehemiah-10:36:3.summary: Numbers 18:12 assigns firstfruits given to the Lord to the priests, the law behind bringing first produce.

nehemiah-10:36:4.summary: Fruit of a planted tree becoming holy to the Lord in its fourth year relates loosely to firstfruit of every tree.

nehemiah-10:36:5.summary: Proverbs urges offering God firstfruits, a general theme rather than a specific link.

nehemiah-10:36:7.summary: Malachi rebukes withholding “the tithes and the firstfruits,” the obligations the people pledge to restore (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:36:8.summary: Numbers 18:2 on Levites joining Aaron's service does not concern firstfruits or the pledge.

nehemiah-10:37:0.summary: Exodus 13:2 consecrates every firstborn, human and animal, to God, the law behind bringing the firstborn of sons and livestock.

nehemiah-10:37:3.summary: Sharing good things with teachers loosely parallels supporting the priests who minister.

nehemiah-10:37:4.summary: Exodus 34:19 claims “every firstborn calf and firstborn sheep,” matching the firstborn of cattle and flocks.

nehemiah-10:37:6.summary: Deuteronomy 12:6 commands bringing “the firstborn of your cattle and of your sheep” to God's place, as pledged here.

nehemiah-10:37:7.summary: Paul argues ministers should share in the offerings they serve, loosely like supplying priests ministering in God's house (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:38:0.summary: Two loaves as firstfruits relate generally to bringing the first offering of grain.

nehemiah-10:38:2.summary: Deuteronomy 26:2 commands bringing the firstfruits of the land to God's chosen place, as pledged for grain and fruit.

nehemiah-10:38:11.summary: Numbers 15 prescribes firstfruits of dough; the Greek here speaks of first offering of grain, a related but looser link.

nehemiah-10:38:12.summary: Malachi 3:8 charges Israel with defrauding God of “the tithes and the firstfruits,” which this pledge restores.

nehemiah-10:38:13.summary: Hezekiah prepared chambers in the Lord's house where firstfruits and tithes were brought under Levite oversight.

nehemiah-10:40:2.summary: Numbers 18:30 concerns the Levites' offering from their tithe as threshing-floor and winepress produce, loosely related.

nehemiah-10:40:3.summary: Deuteronomy 14:23 names bringing tithes “of your grain, and of your wine, and of your oil” to God's place (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:40:4.summary: Deuteronomy 12 commands bringing offerings to God's chosen place, a general link to bringing offerings to the stores (range truncated).

nehemiah-10:40:7.summary: “The house of the Lord our God” in Psalm 121:9 echoes devotion to God's house, a general link.

nehemiah-12:40:3.summary: Rulers gathered and music to God; only a general praise theme.

nehemiah-13:1:1.summary: The people read “from a book of the law”; a general public reading in Nehemiah.

nehemiah-13:15:22.summary: The shown Saints text warns against entering Egypt; no warning language matches Sabbath trade.
nehemiah-13:15:22.why: No real link in Saints text.

nehemiah-13:15:23.summary: Paul testifies against Gentile ways of life; only the verb overlaps.

nehemiah-13:16:0.summary: Sabbath rest extends to “the resident foreigner”; loosely related to outsiders trading on the Sabbath.

nehemiah-13:16:1.summary: The Sabbath includes “the sojourner”; loosely related to outsiders’ Sabbath trade.

nehemiah-13:17:0.summary: “I contended with the commanders,” the same rebuke formula used here.

nehemiah-13:17:1.summary: “I contended with them,” Nehemiah’s same confrontation over marriages.

nehemiah-13:17:2.summary: Rebuke of Israel’s leaders for injustice; general rebuke of leaders.

nehemiah-13:17:3.summary: Warning to Judah’s king and those entering gates (shown portion); general rebuke of leaders.

nehemiah-13:17:4.summary: “I contended with the honored men and leaders,” the same rebuke of Judah’s nobles.

nehemiah-13:17:5.summary: God rebukes unjust judges; general rebuke of rulers.

nehemiah-13:17:6.summary: Those who abandon the law praise impiety; general law-breaking theme.

nehemiah-13:17:7.summary: Rulers of Jacob’s house rebuked; general rebuke of leaders.

nehemiah-13:17:8.summary: Rulers called to attend God’s law; general rebuke of leaders.

nehemiah-13:17:9.summary: The prosperous broke the yoke of God’s law; general rebuke of elites.

nehemiah-13:17:10.summary: A call for the king to be humbled; no link to Sabbath profanation.

nehemiah-13:18:0.summary: Forbids Sabbath burdens “as I commanded your fathers,” who did not hear, the fathers’ sin Nehemiah recalls.

nehemiah-13:18:1.summary: Rising in the fathers’ place “to add still more to the fury” of the Lord against Israel echoes adding wrath against Israel.
nehemiah-13:18:1.why: Same idea of adding to wrath.

nehemiah-13:18:2.summary: Further discipline for continued disobedience; general punishment theme.

nehemiah-13:18:3.summary: Past sin brings “wrath” on “all Israel”; general corporate wrath theme.

nehemiah-13:18:4.summary: “Do not become like your fathers” who did not listen and were overtaken, the same warning from history.

nehemiah-13:18:5.summary: “Have you forgotten your fathers’ evils”; general appeal to the fathers’ sins.

nehemiah-13:18:6.summary: After evils came for their offenses, they return to sin, provoking God; the same argument as here.

nehemiah-13:18:7.summary: Judgment imagery of stripping; no link to Sabbath or fathers.

nehemiah-13:18:9.summary: Allegory of prostitution from Egypt; no link to this verse.

nehemiah-13:18:10.summary: God’s discipline “according to your sins”; general punishment theme.

nehemiah-13:18:11.summary: The land became desolate for wickedness “as on this day”; general consequence theme.
nehemiah-13:18:11.why: Evils that came on the land.

nehemiah-13:18:12.summary: Israelites “profaned the sabbath” under Antiochus; shared phrase but different event.

nehemiah-13:19:0.summary: Sabbath kept “from evening unto evening”; loosely related to closing gates before the Sabbath.

nehemiah-13:19:1.summary: Keeping Sabbaths and the penalty for profaning them; general Sabbath law.

nehemiah-13:19:2.summary: At “Jerusalem’s gates” the people must not lift “burdens on the Sabbath day,” what Nehemiah enforces.

nehemiah-13:19:3.summary: Gleaning law for the poor; no Sabbath or gate link.

nehemiah-13:19:4.summary: “The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened” until a set time, with guards posted, the same measures.

nehemiah-13:21:0.summary: Rulers bear the sword against evil; general authority to punish.

nehemiah-13:21:1.summary: Governors punish evildoers; general enforcement theme.

nehemiah-13:21:2.summary: Judgment on those not obeying God’s law and the king’s; general legal backing for enforcement.

nehemiah-13:21:3.summary: Earlier stage of the same episode: Sabbath traders and Nehemiah’s first warning.

nehemiah-13:22:0.summary: Priests and Levites “were purified” and purified the gatekeepers, as Levites purify themselves to guard the gates.

nehemiah-13:22:1.summary: “Remember me, O God, in this,” the same prayer formula.

nehemiah-13:22:2.summary: “Remember me, our God, for goodness,” the same prayer formula.

nehemiah-13:22:3.summary: Josiah’s removal of Baal vessels; only temple guards overlap loosely.

nehemiah-13:22:4.summary: The king tells the Levites to hymn the Lord; general royal instruction of Levites.

nehemiah-13:22:5.summary: Appeal to God’s atonement rather than strict judgment; general mercy plea.

nehemiah-13:22:6.summary: “Do not enter into judgment with Thy servant”; general plea for mercy.

nehemiah-13:22:7.summary: Levites told to “purify yourselves” and they “purified themselves” for sacred duty, as here.

nehemiah-13:22:8.summary: “Remember me for good, God,” the same prayer of Nehemiah.

nehemiah-13:22:9.summary: “Through the multitude of Thy mercy”; loose echo of “abundance of Thy mercy.”

nehemiah-13:22:10.summary: Priests excluded for lack of genealogy; no link to Sabbath or the prayer.

nehemiah-13:22:11.summary: Hezekiah’s burnt offering with singing; no purification or Sabbath link.

nehemiah-13:22:12.summary: Hezekiah prays “Remember, Lord, how I walked before Thee,” the same plea for God to remember faithful deeds.

nehemiah-13:22:13.summary: “According to the abundance of Thy compassions”; general appeal to abundant mercy.

nehemiah-13:22:14.summary: Levites told to “purify yourselves” for temple service, paralleling purifying Levites here.

nehemiah-13:22:15.summary: Priests make propitiation for all Israel; general sacred-service theme.

nehemiah-13:22:16.summary: “Remember David, Lord” for his zeal for God’s dwelling; loosely like Nehemiah’s plea.

nehemiah-13:22:17.summary: “According to Thy mercy, remember me,” closely matching the plea to remember and spare by God’s mercy.

nehemiah-13:22:18.summary: With the Lord is mercy and abundant redemption; general mercy theme.

nehemiah-13:22:19.summary: High-priestly genealogy; no link to Levites, gates or the prayer.

nehemiah-13:22:20.summary: Kings as foster fathers to Zion; no link to this verse.

nehemiah-13:22:21.summary: “Keep the Sabbath day, to sanctify it,” the command Levites are told to carry out.

nehemiah-13:22:22.summary: Reward awaiting faithful service; loosely like asking God to remember.

nehemiah-13:22:23.summary: Boasting in a clear conscience; general sincerity theme.

nehemiah-13:22:24.summary: God abundantly forgives; general mercy theme.

nehemiah-13:23:1.summary: The covenant not to give or take daughters with “the peoples of the land,” broken by these marriages.

nehemiah-13:23:2.summary: Esdras confronts those who “settled foreign wives,” the same problem.

nehemiah-13:23:3.summary: “Ammanites and Moabites” barred from the assembly, the same peoples of these wives.

nehemiah-13:23:4.summary: Do not be “unequally yoked with unbelievers”; general separation principle.

nehemiah-13:23:5.summary: “All these had taken foreign wives and had fathered sons,” the same situation.

nehemiah-13:23:6.summary: “Do not give your daughters to their sons” or take their daughters, the command broken here.

nehemiah-13:23:7.summary: The Ammanites oppose the wall; same people, different issue.

nehemiah-13:23:8.summary: Ashdod, the city behind “Azotian,” appears, but in an unrelated ark story.

nehemiah-13:24:0.summary: God will change a tongue for peoples; loosely related to children losing Judean speech.

nehemiah-13:25:0.summary: Esdras made Israel “swear” to put away foreign wives, as Nehemiah makes them swear here.

nehemiah-13:25:2.summary: “I contended with the free men,” Nehemiah’s same rebuke formula.

nehemiah-13:25:4.summary: “I contended with the commanders,” Nehemiah’s same rebuke formula.

nehemiah-13:25:5.summary: Nehemiah imposes an oath with a curse on violators, as he curses and makes them swear here.

nehemiah-13:25:6.summary: Warns against taking “their daughters for your sons” and giving yours to theirs, the same prohibition.

nehemiah-13:25:7.summary: “You shall swear by His name”; general oath-by-God theme.

nehemiah-13:25:8.summary: Keeping one’s oath; general theme of honoring oaths.

nehemiah-13:25:9.summary: Judah swore by the Lord in covenant; general covenant oath.

nehemiah-13:25:10.summary: Those who love the law resist the impious; general zeal for the law.

nehemiah-13:25:11.summary: The Saints text has scourges, slaps and spitting, not hair-pulling, so the assumed link is absent.

nehemiah-13:25:12.summary: Discipline for not obeying God’s law and the king’s; general authority for punishment.

nehemiah-13:25:13.summary: Judicial beating of the guilty; loosely like striking offenders.

nehemiah-13:25:14.summary: Levitical curses on lawbreakers (shown portion); general cursing of offenders.

nehemiah-13:25:15.summary: Jesus rebukes law experts for burdens; no link to marriage oath or rebuke here.

nehemiah-13:26:1.summary: Both say no king was like Solomon, “among the kings” in 1 Kings and “no king like him” in Nehemiah.
nehemiah-13:26:1.why: Grounds Nehemiah's claim about Solomon's greatness.

nehemiah-13:26:2.summary: Ecclesiastes warns of a woman who ensnares the sinner; Nehemiah says foreign women turned Solomon aside.
nehemiah-13:26:2.why: General warning about women leading men astray.

nehemiah-13:26:4.summary: God promises Solomon that none like him existed “among the kings,” matching Nehemiah's “no king like him.”
nehemiah-13:26:4.why: Source of the incomparability Nehemiah cites.

nehemiah-13:26:5.summary: Solomon was greater than all kings in wealth and wisdom, the greatness Nehemiah recalls.

nehemiah-13:26:6.summary: Sirach says Solomon “bent your loins toward women,” the same fall Nehemiah cites.
nehemiah-13:26:6.why: Later reflection on Solomon's sin with women.

nehemiah-13:26:7.summary: Sirach says Solomon put a blemish on his glory, describing the fall Nehemiah recalls.
nehemiah-13:26:7.why: Shows the lasting cost of Solomon's sin.

nehemiah-13:27:1.summary: Only the rhetorical question about listening is shared; David's ruling on spoils is unrelated to mixed marriages.

nehemiah-13:28:0.summary: Introduces Sanaballat the Aroni, whose son-in-law Nehemiah drives away.

nehemiah-13:28:1.summary: Sanaballat the Aroni first appears opposing Nehemiah's mission.
nehemiah-13:28:1.why: Explains why marriage to his family was offensive.

nehemiah-13:28:2.summary: Elisoub the high priest, whose grandson married Sanaballat's daughter, leads the building.

nehemiah-13:28:3.summary: Tobia's marriage ties with Judah's leaders parallel the priestly marriage into Sanaballat's family.
nehemiah-13:28:3.why: Another enemy alliance made through marriage.

nehemiah-13:28:4.summary: Lists Eliasib and Joada in the high-priestly line, the same family named in 13:28.
nehemiah-13:28:4.why: Places Joada in the priestly succession.

nehemiah-13:28:6.summary: Paul's teaching on governing authorities has no specific link to Nehemiah expelling the priest.
nehemiah-13:28:6.why: Generic link about rulers punishing evil.

nehemiah-13:28:7.summary: The psalmist removes the lawless from the Lord's city, much as Nehemiah drives out the offender.
nehemiah-13:28:7.why: Royal duty to purge the city.

nehemiah-13:28:8.summary: A wise king winnows the impious, loosely like Nehemiah's expulsion.
nehemiah-13:28:8.why: General proverb on rulers removing wrongdoers.

nehemiah-13:28:9.summary: Eliasib the priest's ties to Tobia are a parallel case of the high-priestly family allied with enemies.

nehemiah-13:28:10.summary: The Greek proverb says no evil stands before a righteous king; nothing ties it specifically to the expulsion.
nehemiah-13:28:10.why: Only a generic idea of royal righteousness.

nehemiah-13:28:11.summary: Same chapter and campaign: Nehemiah contends with those who married foreign wives.

nehemiah-13:29:0.summary: Nehemiah's prayer “Remember, God,” against Tobia and Sanaballat matches “Remember it against them, O God.”

nehemiah-13:29:1.summary: Korah's Levites are rebuked for presuming on the priesthood, loosely related to defiling the priesthood.

nehemiah-13:29:2.summary: Shown verses give priestly purity laws, but the marriage rules are cut off in the truncated range.

nehemiah-13:29:3.summary: Phinehas receives “an everlasting covenant of priesthood,” the covenant Nehemiah says was defiled.

nehemiah-13:29:5.summary: The psalm asks God to have no compassion on the lawless, a loose parallel to Nehemiah's appeal.

nehemiah-13:29:6.summary: God dishonours Eli's priestly house for despising Him, loosely like disqualifying unfaithful priests.
nehemiah-13:29:6.why: Precedent of a priestly house judged.

nehemiah-13:29:7.summary: Malachi condemns profaning “the covenant of your fathers” and devotion to foreign gods in Judah.
nehemiah-13:29:7.why: Contemporary prophetic rebuke of the same offence.

nehemiah-13:29:8.summary: Paul leaves Alexander to the Lord's repayment, like Nehemiah's plea for God to remember wrongdoers.

nehemiah-13:30:0.summary: The covenant pledge not to intermarry with the peoples underlies Nehemiah's purification from foreign ties.
nehemiah-13:30:0.why: The vow the people had broken.

nehemiah-13:30:1.summary: Lists priests and Levites and their service divisions, the order Nehemiah re-established.

nehemiah-13:30:2.summary: David divided the Levites into service courses, the model behind Nehemiah's divisions for priests and Levites.
nehemiah-13:30:2.why: Origin of the priestly service divisions.

nehemiah-13:31:0.summary: Same refrain “Remember me, O God” concerning Nehemiah's good deeds for God's house.

nehemiah-13:31:1.summary: Another “remember me, O God” after reform of the Levites and Sabbath.
nehemiah-13:31:1.why: Same refrain in the same chapter.

nehemiah-13:31:2.summary: The psalmist asks “Remember us, Lord,” a general echo of Nehemiah's prayer.

nehemiah-13:31:3.summary: Love for the Lord's house parallels Nehemiah's care for temple provisions, but without shared wording.

nehemiah-13:31:4.summary: “Remember me ... for Thy kindness’ sake” closely echoes “Remember me, our God, for goodness.”
nehemiah-13:31:4.why: Psalm model for asking God's favourable remembrance.

nehemiah-13:31:6.summary: The thief's “remember me” echoes the wording but in a different setting.
nehemiah-13:31:6.why: Shows the same plea in the Gospel.
